photos.why: Cameron photographed her niece Julia Jackson in an oval, with her face close up and soft. Cameron said she wanted pictures that showed the beauty of a person's thought.
photos.k: How does the soft focus change how you feel about her?

photos.cr: Harriott A. Fox Endowment
photos.why: In 1867 Cameron photographed her niece with her hair loose around her shoulders. Women in Victorian times usually wore their hair up, so this was a bold, artistic choice.
photos.k: Why do you think the hair is loose?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: John Herschel was an astronomer who helped invent photography. He came up with the words photography, negative and positive and discovered how to fix pictures so they would not fade. Cameron photographed him as an old man with wild white hair.
photos.k: Why do you think a scientist's hair looks like that?

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Timothy O'Sullivan traveled with government surveyors across the deserts of the West. Here a wagon team crosses the sand dunes, tiny beside the hills of sand.
photos.k: How would you cross a desert like this?
photos.pr: albumen print from wet collodion negative

photos.t: Syrian Muslim Women in Beirut, City Costume
photos.cr: Gift of William and Margaret Lipscomb
photos.why: Félix Bonfils settled in Beirut with his family and photographed local people in the clothes of the city. Visitors bought these pictures as souvenirs of the Middle East.
photos.k: How could a photograph be a souvenir?
photos.pr: Albumen print from glass plate negative

photos.cr: Gift of Judith K. McMillan
photos.why: Israel Cook Russell photographed the Great Dismal Swamp, a huge wetland on the border of Virginia and North Carolina. Escaped slaves had hidden in its thick forest.
photos.k: Why would it be a good hiding place?

photos.cr: Harriott A. Fox Endowment
photos.why: Julia Margaret Cameron photographed Mary Fisher in 1867. Mary was a close friend and relative who sat for her many times.
photos.k: Why would Cameron photograph the same person again and again?

photos.t: English Tourists at the Mer de Glace, Chamonix
photos.why: Auguste Garcin photographed English tourists walking on the Mer de Glace glacier at Chamonix in 1867. Tourism in the Alps was booming, and visitors wore long dresses and hats to walk on the ice.
photos.k: What would you wear on a glacier?

photos.t: Festival of Ismail Pasha on Board the Ships
photos.why: Gustave Le Gray photographed a party on a ship hosted by Ismail Pasha, the ruler of Egypt, in 1867. Le Gray had gone to Egypt and made pictures there for the court.
photos.k: Why would a ruler throw a party on a ship?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Charles Darwin, who explained evolution in On the Origin of Species, visited Julia Margaret Cameron in 1868. He later said he liked her photograph of him better than any other taken of him.
photos.k: What does his face tell you about his thoughts?

photos.cr: Andrew R. and Martha Holden Jennings Fund
photos.why: Long before his famous horse pictures, Eadweard Muybridge photographed Yosemite under the Greek name "Helios," which means the Sun. His pictures of the tall waterfall made people dream of visiting.
photos.k: How tall do you think the falls are compared with the trees?

photos.t: Have We Not Heard the Bridegroom Is So Sweet
photos.cr: The Mary and Leigh Block Endowment Fund
photos.why: Julia Margaret Cameron staged this photograph from a line of poetry in 1868. She used neighbors and relatives as models, dressed them in costume and let the focus go soft.
photos.k: What mood does the soft focus give the picture?

photos.cr: Smart Family Acquisition Fund
photos.why: Timothy O'Sullivan photographed a volcanic cone at Mono Lake in California in 1868, working for a survey of the American West. He is famous for his strange, empty landscapes.
photos.k: What would you feel standing in such an empty place?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Julia Margaret Cameron photographed the American poet Henry Wadsworth Longfellow in 1868 during his visit to England. His white beard and long hair made him look like a wise old man.
photos.k: What do you think a poet's face looks like?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Joseph Joachim was a Hungarian violinist, one of the greatest of the 1800s. Cameron photographed him in 1868, with the dramatic light and close view she was famous for.
photos.k: What instrument do you play or want to play?

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Jacques-Philippe Potteau photographed working-class girls such as Matra Reinhard in 1868. The pictures were made for scientists who were studying different types of people, and the girls had to stay quite still.
photos.k: How do you think the sitters felt about the scientists?
photos.pr: albumen print from wet collodion negative

photos.why: Charles Marville photographed the narrowest street in Paris, called the Street of the Cat Who Fishes, in 1868. It is only about two meters wide.
photos.k: How could two people pass in a street that narrow?

photos.cr: The Mary and Leigh Block Endowment Fund
photos.why: Julia Margaret Cameron staged scenes from the Bible and legends, using friends and neighbors as models. Soft focus and dramatic light make this picture of an angel feel like a painting.
photos.k: Which parts of the picture look blurry, and why might Cameron want that?

photos.cr: Harriott A. Fox Endowment
photos.why: Cameron photographed this young woman as Elaine, a character in Tennyson's poems about King Arthur. She illustrated the Idylls of the King with her photographs.
photos.k: Which story would you act out for a photograph?

photos.cr: Photography and Media Purchase Fund
photos.why: Cameron borrowed the look of a famous Italian painting of Beatrice Cenci for this portrait. A young woman looks out from under a headcloth, with her eyes soft and thoughtful.
photos.k: Do you think the woman looks happy, sad or both?

photos.cr: Julien Levy Collection, Gift of Jean Levy and the Estate of Julien Levy
photos.why: In the fall of 1870, Paris was surrounded by an enemy army. The city sent mail out by balloon, and Le Neptune lifted off from Montmartre on September 23. Nadar, the balloonist and photographer, organized balloon flights during the siege.
photos.k: What would you put in a balloon mailbag?

photos.t: The Parinirvana of Buddha, Gal Vihara, Polonnaruwa
photos.cr: Gift of Louise S. Richards
photos.why: Joseph Lawton photographed a giant stone Buddha lying down at Polonnaruwa in Sri Lanka. It was carved from a granite cliff about 900 years ago and is 14 meters long.
photos.k: How do you think the sculptors carved something so large?

photos.cr: Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund
photos.why: Auguste Giraudon was a Parisian publisher of photographs who hired artists to pose models as peasants and workers. This man with his walking stick was posed for a series of country types.
photos.k: Why would a publisher use models for a picture of peasants?
photos.pr: albumen print from wet collodion negative

photos.t: Two Shepherdesses Resting with Two Sheep
photos.cr: Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund
photos.why: This staged picture shows two shepherdesses with their sheep. Giraudon sold photographs like this to painters, who used them as models for pictures.
photos.k: Why would a painter use a photograph as a model?
photos.pr: albumen print from wet collodion negative

photos.cr: Jo Hershey Selden Fund
photos.why: Jean Geiser photographed a woman in Algeria in about 1870. Photographers sold such pictures as studies of costume, though a person's own story was often left out.
photos.k: What would you ask her if you could?

photos.cr: Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund
photos.why: Bourne and Shepherd photographed Ranbir Singh, ruler of Jammu and Kashmir, with his sons and court. Their studios took pictures of kings and officials across India.
photos.k: How can you tell who the ruler is?

photos.why: Carleton Watkins photographed the Whitney Glacier and Mount Shasta in California in 1870, from the summit of the smaller peak Shastina. Watkins hauled his huge camera and glass plates up the mountain.
photos.k: Why do you think the glacier is so important to scientists?

photos.why: Francis Frith photographed the cove at Combe Martin on the coast of Devon, England. His pictures were sold in shops across England.
photos.k: What would you do on this beach?

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Amédée Trantoul photographed the village of Castelbouc in the gorge of the Tarn River in southern France. Cliffs tower on both sides.
photos.k: How would you feel living at the bottom of a canyon?
photos.pr: salted paper print from wet collodion negative

photos.cr: Mr. and Mrs. Richard W. Whitehill Art Purchase Endowment Fund
photos.why: Henri Béchard photographed the two enormous seated statues of Pharaoh Amenhotep III at Thebes, Egypt. The statues have been looking over the plain for more than 3,000 years.
photos.k: How would you carve a statue as big as a house?
photos.pr: albumen print from wet collodion negative

photos.why: Timothy O'Sullivan photographed canyons and deserts in the American West in 1871 during an army survey. His pictures show landscapes that many people had never imagined.
photos.k: What would you pack for a trip into the desert?

photos.cr: Gift of Robert A. Taub
photos.why: In 1871 William Henry Jackson joined an expedition to Yellowstone and photographed its geysers. The next year Congress made Yellowstone the first national park, and photographs like this helped persuade lawmakers.
photos.k: What do you think the geyser sounds like?

photos.t: The Paris Fire, Hôtel de Ville
photos.cr: Gift of Frances Hamill
photos.why: In May 1871, during the Paris Commune uprising, fires destroyed the city hall of Paris. Charles Soulier photographed the empty, burned shell of the building.
photos.k: Why would people want to remember a burned building?

photos.why: Oscar Rejlander photographed Charles Darwin, the scientist who explained evolution, seated in profile with his big white beard. Rejlander also took photographs for Darwin's book about emotions.
photos.k: What do you think Darwin is thinking about?

photos.why: Oscar Rejlander photographed a crying child for Charles Darwin's book about emotions. Darwin wanted to show that people everywhere show feelings in the same ways, and photographs helped him prove it.
photos.k: What does your face do when you feel sad?

photos.cr: The Mary and Leigh Block Endowment Fund
photos.why: Julia Margaret Cameron photographed this woman as Balaustion, a Greek heroine in a poem by Robert Browning. She dressed models in costume and let them look away.
photos.k: What do you imagine the heroine is looking at?

photos.why: Timothy O'Sullivan photographed Death Valley in California in 1871, the hottest place in North America. His picture shows pale sand and a few lonely tracks.
photos.k: How would you cross a place that is so hot?

photos.why: Timothy O'Sullivan photographed a high mountain lake in the Sierra Nevada in California in 1871. The still water mirrors the peaks and sky.
photos.k: How does the lake match the mountains?

photos.t: Black Canyon of the Colorado River
photos.why: In 1871 O'Sullivan took a boat up the Colorado River through Black Canyon with a survey team and photographed the walls. He had to haul a darkroom boat through rapids.
photos.k: How would you make a darkroom on a boat?

photos.t: Near the Mouth of the Diamond River
photos.why: O'Sullivan photographed the area near where the Diamond River meets the Colorado in 1871. The rocks stand like walls around the water.
photos.k: What do you see in the rock walls?

photos.t: Valley of the Yosemite from Rocky Ford
photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Muybridge photographed Yosemite's cliffs and the Merced River in the 1870s. The mirrored water makes the valley seem twice as big.
photos.k: What do you notice in the reflections?
photos.pr: albumen print from wet collodion negative

photos.why: Charles Darwin used photographs by Oscar Rejlander in his 1872 book about how people and animals show feelings. These faces show laughing, crying and surprise. It was one of the first science books to use photographs.
photos.k: Make each face yourself. Which emotions are easiest to show?

photos.t: The Bath, a Dripping Spring in Kanab Canyon
photos.cr: Photography Gallery Fund
photos.why: William H. Bell photographed a spring dripping from a canyon wall in Arizona in 1872, with a temperature of 69 degrees. The expedition he joined was exploring the Colorado River.
photos.k: Why would explorers note the temperature of a spring?

photos.t: Canyon of Kanab Wash, Looking South
photos.cr: Gift of William and Margaret Lipscomb
photos.why: Bell was the staff photographer for the 1872 survey of the Colorado River led by John Wesley Powell's team. He photographed the canyon walls rising high on each side.
photos.k: How tall do the canyon walls look?
photos.pr: Albumen print from glass plate negative

photos.why: Oscar Rejlander made photographs for Charles Darwin's 1872 book The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals. This picture was meant to show disgust on a person's face.
photos.k: What is your face like when you taste something yucky?

photos.cr: Photography Gallery Fund
photos.why: Nadar photographed Baron Isidore Taylor, a French art patron who founded groups to help artists. In the 1870s Taylor was an old man with a famous white beard.
photos.k: Why would someone found a group to help artists?
photos.pr: Woodburytype, from the periodical “Galerie Contemporaine Littéraire, Artistique”

photos.cr: Harriott A. Fox Endowment
photos.why: Julia Margaret Cameron photographed George Duckworth, a young man who would be the stepbrother of Virginia Woolf. Cameron photographed her relatives and neighbors in the 1870s.
photos.k: What do you notice about the lighting?

photos.cr: Harriott A. Fox Endowment
photos.why: Cameron photographed Mrs. Rachel Gurney in 1872, a friend, with deep shadows and soft focus. Cameron's pictures were praised by artists but criticized by some for being blurry.
photos.k: Why would an artist choose to blur a picture?

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Lewis Carroll photographed the Arnold sisters in 1872. He liked to take pictures of children and often photographed his friends' daughters.
photos.k: What do you think the sisters thought of Carroll?
photos.pr: albumen print from wet collodion negative

photos.t: Looking South into the Grand Canyon
photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: William H. Bell photographed the Grand Canyon from the north rim in 1872. His photograph shows a huge cliff and the Colorado River far below.
photos.k: How would it feel to stand at the rim?
photos.pr: albumen print from wet collodion negative

photos.t: Hôtel de Ville, Paris, After the Fire
photos.why: Charles Marville photographed the Paris town hall after it was burned in May 1871 by the Paris Commune. Only the stone shell was left, with empty windows.
photos.k: What happens to a city after a fire?

photos.t: Expression of the Emotions, Plate I
photos.why: This photograph was published in Charles Darwin's 1872 book The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals. Darwin used photographs to show how feelings look on faces.
photos.k: What feeling do you think the picture shows?

photos.t: Ancient Ruins in the Cañon de Chelly
photos.cr: Photography Gallery Fund
photos.why: Timothy O'Sullivan photographed a stone house tucked in a canyon wall in Arizona, built about 800 years ago by the ancestors of the Pueblo people. He lowered himself on ropes and used long exposures to catch it.
photos.k: Why would people build homes high up in a cliff?

photos.cr: Photography Gallery Fund
photos.why: El Morro in New Mexico is a rock where travelers carved their names for hundreds of years, from Spanish explorers to settlers. O'Sullivan laid a ruler against the rock to show the size of the inscriptions.
photos.k: Where would you carve your name, and what would you write?
photos.pr: Albumen print, from the album "Geographical & Geological Explorations & Surveys

photos.t: Navajo Life near Old Fort Defiance
photos.cr: Photography Gallery Fund
photos.why: Timothy O'Sullivan photographed Navajo people near Fort Defiance in New Mexico Territory in 1873, after the 1868 treaty let them return to their homeland. The picture shows hogans and daily life.
photos.k: What can you tell about daily life from the picture?
photos.pr: Albumen print, from the album "Geographical & Geological Explorations & Surveys

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: John Thomson photographed a pagoda on an island in the Min River in China. He set up a studio in Hong Kong in 1868 and traveled widely across China, photographing places that few Europeans had seen.
photos.k: Why might a pagoda be on an island?

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Thomson photographed the rapids on the North River in China as boatmen guided a boat. Boat travel was the main way to move around, and the rapids were dangerous.
photos.k: How would you steer a boat through rapids?

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Thomson photographed a monastery in southern China on his journey up the North River. His books of photographs helped Europeans see inland China.
photos.k: What do the roofs and trees look like?

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Étienne Carjat photographed the actress Sarah Bernhardt in 1874 as the heroine of Voltaire's play Zaïre. She was already France's most celebrated actress.
photos.k: How would you pose to look like a tragic heroine?
photos.pr: albumen print from wet collodion negative

photos.cr: Harriott A. Fox Endowment
photos.why: Julia Margaret Cameron moved with her husband to Ceylon (now Sri Lanka) in 1875. Her photographs there show women standing close together in the shade, one balancing a pot.
photos.k: What do you think they were carrying?

photos.cr: Gift of Robert Jesmer
photos.why: Joshua Smith photographed a staged scene, called Good Morning, in the 1870s. Posed scenes were popular and meant to amuse viewers.
photos.k: Who do you think is saying good morning?

photos.cr: Photography Gallery Fund
photos.why: Antoine Samuel Adam-Salomon, a sculptor turned photographer, photographed Émile Angier with dramatic lighting. His portraits looked like carved busts with strong light on one side.
photos.k: Which side of the face is lit?
photos.pr: Woodburytype, from the periodical “Galerie Contemporaine Littéraire, Artistique”

photos.cr: Photography Gallery Fund
photos.why: Jules Armand Dufaure was a French statesman who served as prime minister several times. Adam-Salomon photographed him in the 1870s with sculptural light.
photos.k: How does the light make the face look carved?
photos.pr: Woodburytype, from the periodical “Galerie Contemporaine Littéraire, Artistique”

photos.cr: The A. W. Ellenberger, Sr., Endowment Fund
photos.why: Adolphe Braun photographed the Upper Grindelwald Glacier in the Swiss Alps. Climbing up with big cameras and glass plates was a feat, and his Alpine pictures were popular souvenirs.
photos.k: What shapes do the ice and rock make?
photos.pr: Carbon print, toned, from wet collodion negative

photos.cr: Gift of Catherine Glynn Benkaim and Barbara Timmer
photos.why: This photograph shows a sacred Buddhist site near Colombo in Sri Lanka, perhaps a sacred fig tree planted from a branch of the tree under which Buddha sat. Pilgrims have visited for centuries.
photos.k: Why would a tree be sacred?
photos.pr: Albumen print from glass plate negative

photos.cr: Gift of Michael F. Resch
photos.why: Lai Fong photographed a busy shopping street in Guangzhou, then called Canton, a port city on the Pearl River. The narrow street is crowded with signs, shops and people.
photos.k: What kinds of shops do you see?

photos.cr: Hugh Edwards Photography and Media Purchase Fund
photos.why: Julia Margaret Cameron's handwriting appears in a note on a photograph. She often wrote on the mounts of her pictures and signed them as autographs.
photos.k: Why would an artist write on her own photographs?
photos.pr: Pen and ink, two page, double-sided autograph letter, signed Julia Margaret Came

photos.t: A Creeper in the Peradeniya Gardens, Ceylon
photos.cr: Gift of Catherine Glynn Benkaim and Barbara Timmer
photos.why: Scowen and Company photographed a twisting vine in the botanic gardens of Peradeniya in Sri Lanka. The giant baroque loops of the vine look like sculpture.
photos.k: What does the vine look like?
photos.pr: Albumen print from glass plate negative

photos.t: Entrance to the Nata Dewale Grounds, Kandy
photos.cr: Gift of Catherine Glynn Benkaim and Barbara Timmer
photos.why: Scowen and Company photographed the entrance to a temple site in Kandy, Sri Lanka. Kandy was the last capital of the old kings of Sri Lanka.
photos.k: What would a visitor see on entering?
photos.pr: Albumen print from glass plate negative

photos.cr: Gift of Catherine Glynn Benkaim and Barbara Timmer
photos.why: Scowen and Company photographed fruit sellers in Ceylon, as part of a set of local jobs. Photographs of people at work were popular souvenirs.
photos.k: What fruits do you think they sold?
photos.pr: Albumen print from glass plate negative

photos.why: This is a photograph of Charles Lutwidge Dodgson, who wrote as Lewis Carroll. He was a mathematician at Oxford and a very good photographer.
photos.k: What do you think about the author of Alice looking at you?

photos.cr: Andrew R. and Martha Holden Jennings Fund
photos.why: John Thomson and Adolphe Smith photographed poor families in London for a book called Street Life in London (1877). A convict's home shows the hard life of families left behind.
photos.k: Why would someone make a book about poor people?

photos.cr: Gift of Sharon & Del Zogg in honor of Wendy Watriss and Frederick C. Baldwin (1929-2021), co-founders of Fotofest, Houston, Texas
photos.why: Two men paste a large poster on a wall in London in the late 1870s. Thomson photographed the street trades of London for Street Life in London, and this picture shows how advertising worked before radio and television.
photos.k: How do advertisers reach people today?

photos.cr: Gift of Robert A. Taub
photos.why: John Thomson photographed the people who worked on London's streets, from clowns to chimney sweeps, for his book Street Life in London. It is one of the first books to show ordinary working people in photographs.
photos.k: What kind of job is it to be a street clown?
photos.pr: Woodburytype, from the album "Street Life in London"

photos.cr: Gift of Robert A. Taub
photos.why: A street seller with a donkey cart calls out her berries on a London street. John Thomson and the writer Adolphe Smith made Street Life in London to show the people who earned a living on the streets.
photos.k: How would you advertise fresh strawberries if you were selling them in the street?
photos.pr: Woodburytype, from the album "Street Life in London"

photos.cr: Gift of Robert A. Taub
photos.why: "Crawlers" was a name for the poorest people of London, often elderly women who had no work and wandered the streets. Thomson's photographs made readers see the people behind the word.
photos.k: Why might a picture change how you feel about someone?
photos.pr: Woodburytype, from the album "Street Life in London"

photos.t: When the Day's Work Is Done
photos.cr: Purchased with funds provided by Lucia Woods
photos.why: Henry Peach Robinson arranged this cozy cottage scene with models. A family gathers around a table in warm light at the end of a working day, like a painting made with a camera.
photos.k: What do you think each person is doing after a long day?

photos.cr: Photography Discretionary Fund
photos.why: Some families lived and traveled in wooden wagons, moving through London and the English countryside. John Thomson photographed them in front of their caravan for Street Life in London.
photos.k: What would it be like to live in a wagon?

photos.cr: Photography Discretionary Fund
photos.why: Porters in London's Covent Garden market carried heavy baskets of fruit and vegetables on their heads. Thomson photographed them taking a break.
photos.k: How heavy do you think the baskets were?

photos.cr: Photography Discretionary Fund
photos.why: Thomson photographed women who sold flowers outside Covent Garden market in London. The flower women were a familiar sight and worked in all weather.
photos.k: What flowers might they be selling?

photos.cr: Photography Discretionary Fund
photos.why: Recruiting sergeants stood near Westminster Bridge in London to sign up young men for the army. Thomson photographed them in the 1870s for Street Life in London.
photos.k: How do armies find new soldiers today?

photos.cr: Photography Discretionary Fund
photos.why: Thomson and Adolphe Smith photographed a family whose home was flooded. They wanted readers to see how floods hurt the poor.
photos.k: How would you help a family hit by a flood?

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Raja Deen Dayal photographed the council that ruled Gwalior while its young ruler grew up. Deen Dayal became one of the greatest Indian photographers, and the Nizam of Hyderabad later appointed him court photographer.
photos.k: Why would a young ruler need a council?

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Raja Deen Dayal photographed British officers at Jhansi in India in 1877 for an album. He was the first Indian photographer to become famous across India.
photos.k: What do the officers wear?

photos.t: Judging at the Horse Show at Jhansi
photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Deen Dayal photographed a horse show at Jhansi in India. Horse shows were a favorite way for British and Indian officials to meet.
photos.k: What would the judges look for in a horse?

photos.t: Maharaja Scindia, Nobles and High Officials, Gwalior
photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Raja Deen Dayal photographed the Maharaja of Scindia with nobles and officials at Gwalior in 1877. The group wears rich turbans and jackets.
photos.k: How can you tell which person is the ruler?

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Raja Deen Dayal photographed the viceroy's council at a great meeting in Delhi in 1877. The viceroy governed British India, and the grand event drew hundreds of officials.
photos.k: Why would so many people travel for one meeting?

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Deen Dayal photographed the prized horses of Lord William Beresford in 1877. Beresford was an officer who loved horse racing.
photos.k: Which horse looks the fastest?

photos.t: Rue d'Hautpoul, Entrance to the Quarries
photos.why: Charles Marville photographed the entrance to old stone quarries under Paris in 1877. The city was built from stone mined beneath its streets.
photos.k: What do you think is under a city?

photos.t: Overview of the Quarries, Rue de Compans
photos.why: Marville photographed the area of old quarries and a new market in Paris. As the city grew, it built on top of its old mines.
photos.k: Why would a city build over a quarry?

photos.why: Thomas Edison invented the phonograph, a machine that could record and play back sound, in 1877. This photograph was taken in Mathew Brady's Washington studio after Edison stayed up all night showing it off.
photos.k: What would you record on a phonograph?

photos.cr: Photography Gallery Fund
photos.why: Peter Henry Emerson photographed farm life in Norfolk, England, with a cart piled with hay beside the trees. He wanted photographs that looked the way the human eye sees, a bit soft around the edges.
photos.k: What time of year do you think it is?
photos.pr: Photogravure, Frontispiece from "Pictures of East Anglian Life," published by Sa

photos.why: Eadweard Muybridge lined up cameras along a racetrack so a galloping horse tripped the shutters one after another. The twelve pictures show the horse, Sallie Gardner, with all four hooves off the ground at once.
photos.k: Look at the horse's legs. When are all four hooves off the ground?

photos.why: Leland Stanford, a rich California governor, bet that a galloping horse lifts all four hooves off the ground. Muybridge proved him right with his photographs, and they also helped inspire the first movies.
photos.k: Do the horse's legs look the way painters usually showed them?

photos.why: Eadweard Muybridge photographed San Francisco's big new buildings from above. The wide streets and awnings show a city growing fast after the Gold Rush.
photos.k: What do you see on the street below?

photos.cr: Mr. and Mrs. Richard W. Whitehill Art Purchase Endowment Fund
photos.why: John Burke photographed people involved in the Second Anglo-Afghan War, which began in 1878. He traveled with the army and made one of the first photographic records of Afghanistan.
photos.k: Why would a photographer travel with an army?

photos.t: Amir Yakub Khan and His Officials
photos.cr: Mr. and Mrs. Richard W. Whitehill Art Purchase Endowment Fund
photos.why: John Burke photographed the Afghan ruler Yakub Khan with his advisers. Photographs like this show how leaders posed during a war.
photos.k: What can you tell about the men from their clothes?

photos.cr: Mr. and Mrs. Richard W. Whitehill Art Purchase Endowment Fund
photos.why: John Burke photographed a group of Afridi tribesmen, who live in the mountains between Afghanistan and Pakistan. They were famous fighters.
photos.k: What do you notice about the weapons and clothes?

photos.cr: Mr. and Mrs. Richard W. Whitehill Art Purchase Endowment Fund
photos.why: Burke photographed the village of Lalpura from a ferry on the Kabul River. His pictures show the landscape through which the army traveled.
photos.k: What would it be like to cross a river on a ferry?

photos.t: View from the Top of the Rock, Trichinopoly
photos.cr: Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund
photos.why: Nicholas and Company photographed the city of Trichinopoly, now Tiruchirappalli, in India, from the top of the great rock. Below you can see the town and the Ranganathaswamy Temple.
photos.k: How many temple towers can you spot?

photos.cr: Photography Gallery Fund
photos.why: Nadar photographed Eugène Viollet-le-Duc, the architect who restored Notre-Dame cathedral in Paris. He rebuilt towers and added the spire.
photos.k: What does an architect who rebuilds castles do all day?
photos.pr: Woodburytype, from the periodical “Galerie Contemporaine Littéraire, Artistique”

photos.cr: Mr. and Mrs. Richard W. Whitehill Art Purchase Endowment Fund
photos.why: John Burke photographed General Frederick Roberts and his staff during the Second Anglo-Afghan War in 1878. Roberts led the march to Kabul.
photos.k: What do the soldiers' uniforms look like?

photos.cr: Mr. and Mrs. Richard W. Whitehill Art Purchase Endowment Fund
photos.why: John Burke photographed a river gorge near Lalpura on the Kabul River in 1878. The cliffs rise on both sides of the water.
photos.k: What would crossing the gorge be like?

photos.cr: Mr. and Mrs. Richard W. Whitehill Art Purchase Endowment Fund
photos.why: John Burke photographed the army camp at Landi Kotal in the Khyber Pass in 1878. Tents stretch across the high valley.
photos.k: Why would a camp be set up in a pass?

photos.t: Chinak, Looking Toward the Kurram River
photos.cr: Mr. and Mrs. Richard W. Whitehill Art Purchase Endowment Fund
photos.why: John Burke photographed the area near the Kurram River in Afghanistan in 1878. The wide valley is marked by mountains in the distance.
photos.k: How far do you think the mountains are?

photos.cr: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Douglas Kenyon
photos.why: L. A. Huffman lived in Miles City, Montana, and photographed Native people, cowboys and the great plains. This portrait of a Cheyenne woman, her braids neatly hanging, was made when the old ways of life on the plains were changing quickly.
photos.k: What do you notice about her clothes and hair?

photos.why: Frederick Douglass was a leader in the fight to end slavery and win equal rights. In this portrait taken around 1879, he is in his sixties with a full white beard and a calm gaze.
photos.k: What does his steady look tell you?

photos.cr: John Cook Memorial Fund
photos.why: Étienne Carjat, a celebrated Paris photographer, made this portrait of a couple. They paid extra to have it fired onto enamel, a more permanent finish.
photos.k: Why would they want their portrait to last longer?
photos.pr: Photograph on enamel in copper alloy frame with velvet liner

photos.t: Plaster Cast of a Body, Pompeii
photos.cr: Gift of W. Bruce and Delaney H. Lundberg
photos.why: When Mount Vesuvius erupted in 79 AD, ash buried the city of Pompeii. Later, archaeologists poured plaster into the hollows left by bodies, creating casts like this one. Giorgio Sommer photographed them for visitors.
photos.k: How can an empty space in ash tell us what a person looked like?

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Frank Jay Haynes photographed Devil's Slide, a stripe of red rock on a mountain near Yellowstone National Park, in 1880. Haynes later became the official photographer of Yellowstone.
photos.k: What makes the red stripe look so strange?
photos.pr: albumen print from wet collodion negative

photos.cr: Purchase from the Karl B. Goldfield Trust
photos.why: European photographers in the colonies often made portraits of the local people, and they sold them to visitors. This woman from Ceylon, now Sri Lanka, stands in the dress of her village.
photos.k: How could a photograph hide a person's own story?

photos.cr: Purchase from the Karl B. Goldfield Trust
photos.why: A Sinhalese man wears a Western jacket and shirt, but he keeps his traditional hairstyle. His clothes show how two cultures mixed in Ceylon in the 1800s.
photos.k: Which parts of his clothes come from which culture?

photos.cr: Purchase from the Karl B. Goldfield Trust
photos.why: The Veddahs are an indigenous people of Sri Lanka, who for centuries lived by hunting and gathering in the forests. Photographers in the 1880s visited them as a curiosity.
photos.k: Why do you think they were famous with visitors?

photos.cr: Purchase from the Karl B. Goldfield Trust
photos.why: British officials and their families relaxed at a bungalow on a leisurely afternoon in India. Photographs like this show how colonial life looked to those who lived it.
photos.k: What would you do on a leisurely afternoon without screens?

photos.why: This is a portrait of Bernt Askevold, a Norwegian painter, around 1880. Many of these portraits were saved by regional archives in Norway.
photos.k: Why would an archive keep old portraits?

photos.why: This photograph shows Roald Amundsen as an eight-year-old boy around 1880. He grew up to be the first person to reach the South Pole in 1911.
photos.k: What do you think a polar explorer looked like as a child?

photos.why: A boy poses with his rocking horse in a Norwegian photo studio around 1880. Studios had toy horses as props for children.
photos.k: What toy would you bring?

photos.why: Two boys in matching outfits pose in a Norwegian studio around 1880. Brothers were often dressed alike for portraits.
photos.k: Why would parents dress brothers the same?

photos.t: Group on a Beach with Three Babies
photos.why: This ferrotype, a photograph on thin metal, shows a group with three babies on a beach around 1880. Beach photographers set up tents to make quick portraits for visitors.
photos.k: How would a photographer work on a beach?

photos.why: A seated girl in a checked dress poses in a Norwegian studio. Her dress pattern shows how clothes looked in the 1880s.
photos.k: How does the checked pattern look in a black-and-white picture?

photos.t: Church of the Holy Sepulchre, Jerusalem
photos.why: Luigi Fiorillo photographed a religious ceremony at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem in the 1880s. Pilgrims from around the world came to this holy place.
photos.k: Why would people travel so far?

photos.why: This tintype of the outlaw Billy the Kid was taken around 1880 in New Mexico. It is the only authenticated photograph of him, and he holds a rifle and wears a hat. He was killed in 1881 at age 21.
photos.k: Why do people remain fascinated by outlaws?

photos.cr: Gift of Michael F. Resch
photos.why: The London Stereoscopic Company photographed Hong Lim Green, an open space in the Chinese district of Singapore, in 1882. The Chinese were the biggest ethnic group in Singapore, which was a busy port.
photos.k: What do you think the open space was used for?

photos.cr: Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund
photos.why: Raja Deen Dayal made a two-part panorama of the Narmada River at the temple island of Omkareshwar in India. He placed the river in front of the camera and joined two plates for a wide view.
photos.k: How does joining two pictures make a wide view?

photos.t: The Head of the Statue of Liberty
photos.why: In Paris, the giant head of the Statue of Liberty stood in a yard while the rest of the statue was built. The statue was later taken apart and shipped to New York in crates.
photos.k: How tall are the people standing beside the head?

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Louise Deshong Woodbridge, a Philadelphia socialite, photographed the boat house of the famous actor Edwin Booth in Newport, Rhode Island, on August 6, 1884. She was an amateur with a good eye.
photos.k: Why would a rich actor have a boat house?
photos.pr: albumen print from gelatin dry plate negative

photos.why: Eadweard Muybridge photographed an elephant walking, with cameras set to snap one after another. His series of animals in motion in the 1880s helped people see how bodies move.
photos.k: How does the elephant move its legs?

photos.cr: Gift of Michael D. Willis
photos.why: The Kailasa temple in India was carved out of a single hillside of rock, from the top down. Raja Deen Dayal photographed its carved columns and towers.
photos.k: How could people carve a whole temple out of one rock?

photos.cr: Edwin R. and Harriet Pelton Perkins Memorial Fund
photos.why: Frank Jay Haynes photographed a steaming hot spring at Yellowstone National Park in 1885. The colors in the pool come from heat-loving microbes, but black-and-white pictures could only show the steam and shapes.
photos.k: What would the colors be like in real life?

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Thomas Eakins, the American painter, photographed children outside in the 1880s. He used photography to study how bodies and light look, as a help for his paintings.
photos.k: How is a photograph useful for a painter?

photos.cr: Gift of Catherine Glynn Benkaim and Barbara Timmer
photos.why: A Swiss firm printed this view of the mosque of Aurangzeb, the sixth Mughal emperor, in Benares, now Varanasi. The mosque stands high above the Ganges, with tall minarets.
photos.k: What do you notice about the mosque's towers?

photos.t: Clara L. White as a Child
photos.cr: Gift of Nina Rosenblum and Lisa Rosenblum
photos.why: This small portrait of a girl named Clara L. White is a photograph painted by hand with colors. The painter's skill gives it an intimate and glowing look.
photos.k: Why would someone paint over a photograph?
photos.pr: Matte collodion with hand-applied crayon and paint

photos.cr: Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund
photos.why: Raja Deen Dayal photographed the ruined college of Mahmud Gawan in Bidar, India, built in the 1400s. The tower's pattern echoes designs on Bidri metalwork.
photos.k: What patterns do you see on the tower?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Washington Monument in Washington, D.C., was dedicated on February 21, 1885. A huge crowd gathered at its base, and at 555 feet it was the tallest structure in the world for a while.
photos.k: What do you think the day was like?

photos.t: Likely Patrick J. Norton and Siblings
photos.why: This photograph shows a family of children, most likely Patrick Norton and his siblings, around 1885. Studio portraits like this were treasured by families.
photos.k: What do you think the children are feeling?

photos.cr: Ada Turnbull Hertle Fund
photos.why: Men carry bundles of reeds home across the marshes of the Norfolk Broads. Emerson made soft-focus pictures like this to show the beauty of a vanishing way of life.
photos.k: What did people use reeds for?
photos.pr: Platinum print, pl. I from the album "Life and Landscape on the Norfolk Broads"

photos.cr: Ada Turnbull Hertle Fund
photos.why: Two people gather water lilies from a small boat among the reeds of the Norfolk Broads. Emerson's pictures of this watery landscape became famous and made photographers think about how the eye really sees.
photos.k: What do you think they will do with the lilies?
photos.pr: Platinum print, pl. IX from the album "Life and Landscape on the Norfolk Broads"

photos.cr: Ada Turnbull Hertle Fund
photos.why: Workers on the Norfolk Broads pole a flat boat loaded with marsh hay. Peter Henry Emerson published this picture in a book of photographs of East Anglian life.
photos.k: What do you think the hay was used for?
photos.pr: Platinum print, pl. XVII from the album "Life and Landscape on the Norfolk Broad

photos.cr: Julien Levy Collection, Gift of Jean Levy and the Estate of Julien Levy
photos.why: The chemist Michel-Eugène Chevreul turned a hundred in 1886, and Paul Nadar, Nadar's son, photographed him as he talked. The pictures were published with his words in a newspaper, the first photo-interview ever.
photos.k: What would you ask someone who is a hundred years old?

photos.why: Paul Nadar's series of Chevreul gesturing and speaking was printed with captions of his words. It was the first time a newspaper used photographs to tell an interview, and it is the grandfather of today's video interviews.
photos.k: Which of his expressions do you like best?

photos.t: His Highness the Maharaja of Rewa
photos.cr: Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund
photos.why: Raja Deen Dayal photographed the Maharaja of Rewa in 1886. Being an Indian photographer may have helped him get access to rulers and their courts.
photos.k: Why might a ruler trust a local photographer?

photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed himself in Freienwalde, Germany, in 1886 when he was a young student. He later became the great champion of photography as art in America.
photos.k: Why would a student photograph himself?

photos.why: Peter Henry Emerson photographed a cottage of a Norfolk Broads worker in 1886. Platinum prints give a soft, lasting gray tone.
photos.k: What would living on the Broads be like?

photos.why: Emerson photographed a boat-yard on the Norfolk Broads in 1886. Workers build wooden boats, which are used to carry reeds and cargo.
photos.k: How would you build a wooden boat?

photos.why: Emerson photographed a wildfowl hunter creeping toward ducks in a punt on the Broads in 1886. Hunters had to be very quiet to get near.
photos.k: How would you sneak up on a bird?

photos.why: Emerson photographed a farm in the marsh of Norfolk in 1886. Flat land and pale sky show how big the open land is.
photos.k: What would farming a marsh be like?

photos.why: Emerson photographed a misty autumn morning in the English countryside in 1886. He used soft focus to match the way the human eye sees.
photos.k: What do you hear on a misty morning?

photos.why: Thomas Frederick Goodall, a friend of Emerson, helped make this picture of a boat in the shallow water of the Broads in 1886. The title means between land and water.
photos.k: Where does the land end and the water begin?

photos.why: Emerson photographed workers bringing in the barley harvest in the 1880s. He disliked posed pictures, and this one shows ordinary work.
photos.k: What jobs can you see?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: A road lined with bare trees runs into the distance on a cold day. Alfred Stieglitz was a young student in Germany when he made this quiet picture and began to love photography.
photos.k: What season does it feel like?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed wide stone steps leading down to the water in Chioggia, Italy. The sunlight and smooth stone make a simple, calm picture.
photos.k: Where do you think the steps lead?

photos.cr: Gift of Phyllis Seltzer in memory of John Cook
photos.why: Muybridge photographed horses and other animals at the University of Pennsylvania in the 1880s and published hundreds of plates as Animal Locomotion. Each row of small pictures shows a horse moving a step at a time.
photos.k: Count the frames. Which one shows a hoof on the ground?

photos.why: This plate from Animal Locomotion shows a bison walking, step by step. Muybridge photographed animals at the Philadelphia Zoo, and artists and scientists used his plates to study how bodies move.
photos.k: How does the buffalo's head move as it walks?

photos.cr: Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund
photos.why: Raja Deen Dayal photographed Mrs. and Miss Lyall in Shimla, India, in 1887. Many of his Shimla portraits include rickshaws, which were the way to get around the hill town.
photos.k: How is a rickshaw different from a car?

photos.why: Peter Henry Emerson published this photograph in his 1887 book Pictures from Life in Field and Fen. It shows a fisherman in his home in the English fens.
photos.k: What does a fisherman's home look like?

photos.t: At Plough, the End of the Furrow
photos.why: A farmer turns his plough and horses at the end of the field in Emerson's 1887 book. Emerson photographed rural life in England as it was disappearing.
photos.k: How would you plough a field with horses?

photos.why: Peter Henry Emerson photographed a cold winter's morning in the English fens in 1887. The soft light and mist are typical of his natural style.
photos.k: What do you hear on a quiet winter morning?

photos.why: Emerson photographed a dame school, a small village school run by an old woman, in his 1887 book. Children learned reading and writing in the dame's own kitchen.
photos.k: What would a school in a kitchen be like?

photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed two Italian men laughing together in the street in Bellagio, in 1887. It shows his early love of everyday life and won a prize in a photography contest.
photos.k: What might the joke be?

photos.cr: Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund
photos.why: Raja Deen Dayal photographed a picnic party in Mashobra near Shimla in 1887. British officials and their families held lavish outdoor parties in the hills.
photos.k: What would you bring to a picnic in the hills?

photos.cr: Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund
photos.why: Raja Deen Dayal photographed Robert Hotz, a professional photographer, with his bulldog in 1887. Hotz was a competitor who lived in Shimla.
photos.k: Why would a photographer pose with his dog?

photos.t: Colonel Thuillier and His Wife Emmeline
photos.cr: Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund
photos.why: Deen Dayal photographed Colonel Thuillier and his wife Emmeline in 1887. Large group portraits and couples brought him regular work.
photos.k: What can you tell about the couple?

photos.why: Emerson photographed old fishermen at a hospital for retired fishermen in Great Yarmouth in 1887. The men sit quietly in their uniform and caps.
photos.k: What stories might the old fishermen tell?

photos.why: Emerson photographed a scene called Confessions in his book Pictures from Life in Field and Fen in 1887. He used everyday people and a natural, quiet look.
photos.k: What do you think the title means?

photos.cr: Photography Gallery Fund
photos.why: A farmer guides two horses pulling a plow across a big field under a gray sky. Peter Henry Emerson wanted to show the strength and beauty of working life in the English countryside.
photos.k: How do you think the farmer and horses feel at the end of the day?
photos.pr: Photogravure, plate IV from "Pictures of East Anglian Life," published by Sampso

photos.cr: Photography Gallery Fund
photos.why: Two boys stop on a path in the marshes of Norfolk to look at a toad. Emerson's photographs from East Anglia caught everyday moments of country life.
photos.k: What would you do if you found a toad on your path?
photos.pr: Photogravure, pl. XXVII from the album "Pictures of East Anglian Life" (1888)

photos.cr: Gift of Flora Stieglitz Straus
photos.why: A big family gathers on a porch and steps at Lake George, New York. Alfred Stieglitz's family owned a summer home there, and it later became his favorite place to photograph.
photos.k: How many people can you count?

photos.why: Louis-Émile Durandelle photographed the Eiffel Tower as its iron legs rose above Paris. It was finished in March 1889 and was the tallest structure in the world, at about 300 meters.
photos.k: How many levels does the tower have so far?

photos.why: Jacob Riis photographed a narrow alley in New York's Mulberry Bend, one of the roughest slums in the city. He used flash powder, which produced a sudden bang and light, so people in his pictures often look startled.
photos.k: What do you notice about the people's faces?

photos.t: Baby in a Slum Tenement Hallway
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A baby crawls on the floor in a hallway of a crowded New York tenement. Riis's pictures showed readers that children were growing up in dark, cramped buildings.
photos.k: What would you change about this hallway?

photos.cr: Gift of Flora Stieglitz Straus
photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed a snowy street in Berlin in 1888 while he was a student in Germany. He loved difficult conditions such as snow and rain.
photos.k: How does snow change a city?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed a young woman writing at a table beside a window, with the sunlight forming stripes. It was one of his first pictures to win notice, and it shows that a photographer can paint with light.
photos.k: Where does the sunlight fall in the room?

photos.why: In this crowded tenement room in New York's Bayard Street, lodgers paid five cents a night for a spot to sleep on the floor. Jacob Riis made the picture with flash powder, and it helped convince New Yorkers to improve housing.
photos.k: How many people can you spot sleeping in the room?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Families from Bohemia (now part of the Czech Republic) rolled cigars at home in their tiny New York apartments, working for very little pay. Riis photographed them in their cramped kitchen workroom.
photos.k: What would it be like to work where you live?

photos.t: Sweatshop in a Ludlow Street Tenement
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Men, women and children sewed clothes in crowded rooms, often for long hours. Riis's pictures of sweatshops showed the hidden work behind the clothes people bought.
photos.k: What can you tell about their jobs from the room?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A family gathers in a dark basement room in a poor corner of New York called Poverty Gap. Jacob Riis wrote that the room was damp and dim, and that children lived there year-round.
photos.k: What would you want for this family?

photos.why: Édouard Baldus made a photogravure, a print from a photograph, of the Romanesque church of Saint-Julien in Brioude, France. Photogravures turned photographs into ink prints for books.
photos.k: How could you make a printed book from a photograph?

photos.t: A Street in Sterzing, the Tyrol
photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed a narrow street in an old Austrian town, with bright sun on one side and deep shadow on the other. The line between light and dark gives the picture its mood.
photos.k: Where would you walk to stay in the shade?

photos.why: Raja Lala Deen Dayal was one of India's most famous photographers, appointed to photograph the Nizam of Hyderabad. This portrait shows him in a white turban, calm and confident.
photos.k: What would a photographer need to carry around India in the 1880s?

photos.cr: Gift of Robert A. Taub
photos.why: Étienne-Jules Marey photographed a man on a bicycle in motion around 1890. Marey, a scientist, invented the chronophotograph that records movement in a single plate.
photos.k: How does the camera show motion in one picture?

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Robert Stuart Redfield photographed Mount Washington in Massachusetts on July 22, 1890. Redfield was a leading amateur of his day, and he later became a driving force of art photography.
photos.k: What time of year do you think this is?

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Paul Géniaux photographed porters carrying baskets of fish in the 1890s. Géniaux took many pictures of working people in France.
photos.k: How heavy would the baskets be?

photos.cr: Jo Hershey Selden Fund
photos.why: A. W. A. Plâté Studio photographed the Jain Temple in Calcutta, now Kolkata, in the 1890s. The temple is decorated with mirrors, glass and gardens.
photos.k: What does a temple look like when it is covered in mirrors?

photos.cr: Mr. and Mrs. Roger J. Lerch in Memory of Carl J. Lerch and Winifred J. Lerch Endowment
photos.why: Peter Henry Emerson photographed reeds and weeds on the marsh for a book of etchings from photographs in 1890. His late work was softer and more artistic.
photos.k: How do soft pictures feel different?

photos.cr: Mr. and Mrs. Roger J. Lerch in Memory of Carl J. Lerch and Winifred J. Lerch Endowment
photos.why: Emerson's last book of photographs, Marsh Leaves, included this winter sunrise. He used a delicate gravure to catch the sky.
photos.k: What time is it in the picture?

photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed a snowy street from his window in Berlin around 1890. Stieglitz, who studied there, loved the changing light and weather.
photos.k: What can you see from your window?

photos.why: Thomas Smillie was the Smithsonian Institution's first photographer. He photographed objects, scientists and expeditions for the museum.
photos.k: Why would a museum need its own photographer?

photos.why: This tintype shows Honus Wagner, who would become one of baseball's greatest shortstops. Wagner started playing professionally in the 1890s.
photos.k: Why would a baseball star's old tintype be treasured?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Detroit Publishing Company made this photochrom of Hohen Kasten, a mountain in Appenzell, Switzerland, in the 1890s. A photochrom turns a black-and-white photograph into a color print using lithographic stones.
photos.k: How could color be added to a black-and-white picture?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: This photochrom shows the Zytglogge clock tower in Bern, Switzerland. The tower has a clock with moving figures that put on a show every hour.
photos.k: What would you see when the clock strikes?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A photochrom shows the Urseren Valley, a high Alpine valley in Switzerland, with green meadows and mountains. Photochroms made the Alps look like paintings.
photos.k: What do you notice about the colors?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: This Detroit Publishing photochrom shows the Devil's Bridge in the Schöllenen Gorge in Switzerland. Legend says the Devil built it in exchange for the first soul to cross.
photos.k: Would you cross a bridge built by the Devil?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A photochrom of the seaside town of Aberdovey in Wales in the 1890s. Photochrom prints were sold to tourists as vivid souvenirs.
photos.k: What do you think a day at the beach in 1890 was like?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: This photochrom, made by the Detroit Publishing Company in the 1890s, shows a rocky pass in Snowdonia, Wales, where a river runs between steep wooded slopes. Photochroms were color prints made from black-and-white photographs using inked stones.
photos.k: How do you think color was added to a black-and-white photo?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Pont-y-Pair is an old stone bridge over the River Llugwy in north Wales, and tourists loved to visit it. This photochrom shows the water rushing among the rocks under the arches.
photos.k: How many arches do you see?

photos.t: Cadair Idris and the Dysynni Valley
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: This photochrom shows Cadair Idris, a mountain in Wales, rising above a valley with cattle grazing. Welsh legend says anyone who sleeps on the mountain wakes up a poet or a madman.
photos.k: Would you try sleeping on Cadair Idris?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: This photochrom, made about 1890, shows Snowdon, the highest mountain in Wales, rising behind a road. Printed in many colors, it was sold to tourists.
photos.k: How high do you think the mountain is?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: This is Abbotsford, the house of the author Sir Walter Scott, as seen from the River Tweed in Scotland. Scott's novels made Scotland a favorite place for tourists.
photos.k: Why would readers visit a writer's house?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Black Watch Monument near Aberfeldy in Scotland honors a Highland regiment. A soldier in a kilt stands on top, and this photochrom shows it in the countryside.
photos.k: Why do monuments often have a soldier standing on top?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Ailsa Craig is a rocky island that rises out of the sea off the coast of Scotland. It is famous for its granite, which is used to make curling stones.
photos.k: What do you think the island is like up close?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A young Irish girl, called a colleen, poses for a photochrom made by the Detroit Publishing Company. Pictures of country people were popular with tourists in the 1890s.
photos.k: What is she wearing?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A jaunting car is a light two-wheeled carriage where passengers sit back to back, used in Ireland. This photochrom shows tourists' favorite way of getting around.
photos.k: Would you like to ride in a jaunting car?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Cliffs of Moher in Ireland rise about 200 meters above the Atlantic Ocean. This photochrom from the 1890s shows the towering cliffs.
photos.k: How tall are 200 meters compared with a building?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A photochrom of the Eccles Hotel in Glengarriff, County Cork, Ireland. The hotel was popular with tourists who came for the mild climate and the harbor.
photos.k: Why do people stay in hotels when they travel?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: This photograph shows a farm in a valley in Connecticut around 1890. Barns and trees spread across the hills of rural New England.
photos.k: What do you think a farm morning is like?

photos.cr: Gift of Robert A. Taub
photos.why: Frederick H. Evans photographed the carved doorway of Ely Cathedral in England, with a tiny figure standing inside. He loved cathedrals and waited for the best light, and he never touched up his pictures.
photos.k: How does the small person make the doorway feel bigger?

photos.cr: Gift of Judith Barter in memory of Frederick J. and Emily M. Barter
photos.why: Benjamin West Kilburn made a stereograph of the excavations at Pompeii, the Roman town buried by the volcano Vesuvius in the year 79. Digging uncovered streets and houses just as people left them.
photos.k: What would you find if you dug up a whole town?

photos.t: Zacatecas from Below the Railroad Station
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Detroit Publishing Company photographed the old mining city of Zacatecas, Mexico, in the 1890s. The city of silver mines lies in a bowl of hills.
photos.k: Why do mining towns grow in hills?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: This panorama shows Guanajuato, a colorful city in Mexico built in a narrow valley, in the 1890s. Houses of every color climb the hillsides.
photos.k: How would you get around in a city built on hills?

photos.cr: Gift of Daniel, Richard, and Jonathan Logan
photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed a narrow Venetian canal, where houses and boats double in the water. Reflections became one of his favorite subjects.
photos.k: Where does the building end and its reflection begin?

photos.cr: Gift of Daniel, Richard, and Jonathan Logan
photos.why: Charles I. Berg made this photograph, number 5 in the portfolio American Pictorial Photography, in 1892. Pictorialists aimed to make photographs look like paintings, with soft focus and moody poses.
photos.k: Why would a photographer want a photo to look like a painting?

photos.t: Wet Night, Columbus Circle, New York
photos.cr: Gift of Daniel, Richard, and Jonathan Logan
photos.why: William A. Fraser photographed a rainy night at Columbus Circle in New York in 1892. Wet streets and glowing lights give a mood that painters loved.
photos.k: What do rain and lights do to a street at night?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: This photograph shows the granite tomb of the poet Walt Whitman in Camden, New Jersey, around 1892. He designed the stone house-like tomb himself before he died.
photos.k: Why would someone plan their own tomb?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: On a snowy day in New York, a driver blankets his horse at the end of the streetcar line. Alfred Stieglitz took this picture with a hand camera in a storm, and it became one of the first great photographs of city life.
photos.k: What are the horses wearing to keep warm?

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: William H. Rau photographed Bear Lake in Pennsylvania in 1893. Railroads hired photographers to take scenic pictures to attract tourists.
photos.k: Why would a railroad want pretty pictures?
photos.pr: albumen print from gelatin dry plate negative

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: A woman in a white cap mends fishing nets on the dunes of the Dutch coast. Stieglitz traveled around Europe in the 1890s photographing ordinary people at their work.
photos.k: What jobs do people do at the sea?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Mountain peaks rise above a sea of cloud and snow in the Alps. Stieglitz photographed Europe's mountains while he traveled as a young man.
photos.k: How would you climb a mountain like this?

photos.t: A Wet Day on the Boulevard, Paris
photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Rain makes the Paris street shine like glass. Stieglitz loved bad weather, which other photographers avoided, and he showed that rain, mist and snow could be beautiful.
photos.k: What do you notice about the wet street?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Two people in long shawls hurry along a Dutch beach toward a church as the weather turns. Stieglitz photographed this on a trip to the Netherlands.
photos.k: What do you think they are hurrying away from?

photos.why: Queen Victoria sits with dozens of her children, grandchildren and their families. Several became kings and queens in other countries, which is why people called her the grandmother of Europe.
photos.k: How many people can you count in the picture?

photos.why: A photographer made this picture of women mending nets in Katwijk, a fishing town in the Netherlands, in 1894. Nets needed constant repair, and women often did the job.
photos.k: How would you mend a big net?

photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed workers harvesting in the Black Forest in Germany in 1894. He wanted to show the beauty of ordinary work.
photos.k: What are the people doing in the field?

photos.why: Alexander Graham Bell was born in Scotland and invented the telephone in 1876. He also taught deaf children to speak and spent his life inventing.
photos.k: What would you ask someone who invented the telephone?

photos.why: Arnold Genthe photographed San Francisco's Chinatown with a hidden camera, because many people there feared cameras. In this picture, a woman and children take a stroll in their holiday best.
photos.k: Why might some people have been afraid of cameras?

photos.cr: Gift of John Flory, Elizabeth Flory Kelly, and Phoebe Flory
photos.why: Clarence H. White photographed a quiet winter landscape in about 1895. White was a leading pictorialist who later taught many great photographers.
photos.k: What sound does a winter field make?

photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: William B. Post photographed landscapes in Vermont around the turn of the 20th century. He often photographed in snow.
photos.k: Why would a photographer like winter?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: This monument at Oakwood Cemetery in Chicago was dedicated in 1895 to Confederate soldiers who died in a prison camp. It towers over the graves.
photos.k: Why would a cemetery have a big monument?

photos.cr: Gift of John Flory, Elizabeth Flory Kelly, and Phoebe Flory
photos.why: Clarence H. White photographed his wife by a window, with soft light on her profile. He and his friends believed a photograph could be gentle and poetic.
photos.k: What might she see outside?
photos.pr: platinum print with watercolor and gouache

photos.t: A Merchant and His Servant, Chinatown
photos.why: A Chinese merchant in a long robe poses with a younger attendant in San Francisco's Chinatown. Genthe made hundreds of pictures of the neighborhood before the 1906 earthquake destroyed it.
photos.k: What do their clothes tell you about their roles?

photos.t: Meeting of Day and Night, Lake George
photos.cr: Gift of Flora Stieglitz Straus
photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed a scene at Lake George, New York, in 1896. The title describes the hour between sunset and darkness, when light fades.
photos.k: What colors does the sky turn between day and night?

photos.cr: Gift of John Flory, Elizabeth Flory Kelly, and Phoebe Flory
photos.why: Clarence H. White photographed a quiet canal in Ohio in 1896. A woman and a path run alongside the water in soft light.
photos.k: What does a canal path feel like?

photos.cr: Gift of John Flory, Elizabeth Flory Kelly, and Phoebe Flory
photos.why: Clarence H. White photographed this posed picture of a woman writing, with the title What Shall I Say? in 1896. White made quiet scenes of family life in Newark, Ohio.
photos.k: What do you think she is writing?

photos.cr: Gift of Amy and Neil Viny
photos.why: Maurice Loewy and Pierre Puiseux photographed the Moon through a telescope at the Paris Observatory in the 1890s. Their huge atlas of the Moon helped astronomers map its craters.
photos.k: How do astronomers map the Moon?

photos.t: Arnold Genthe with a Woman Friend
photos.why: Arnold Genthe photographed himself seated outdoors with a woman friend in the 1890s. Genthe was a German-born photographer who settled in San Francisco.
photos.k: Why would a photographer be photographed?

photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed Kikisoblu, called Princess Angeline, in Seattle in 1896. She was the daughter of Chief Sealth, for whom Seattle is named, and she lived in a small house on the waterfront. This portrait was one of Curtis's first big successes.
photos.k: Why would a famous photographer pick her as a subject?

photos.t: A Chinese Boy, Chinatown, San Francisco
photos.why: Arnold Genthe photographed a boy in San Francisco's Chinatown in the 1890s. Genthe made hundreds of secret pictures of the neighborhood with a hidden camera.
photos.k: What do you think the boy is looking at?

photos.why: Genthe photographed a group of friends including the poet George Sterling, the writer Mary Austin and Jack London. Writers loved to visit his studio in Carmel.
photos.k: Why would writers be friends with a photographer?

photos.cr: Gift of John Flory, Elizabeth Flory Kelly, and Phoebe Flory
photos.why: Two women sit close, absorbed in a book by the window. Clarence H. White arranged simple scenes of family life in soft light.
photos.k: What book do you think they are reading?

photos.why: Leo Tolstoy wrote War and Peace and Anna Karenina, two of the most famous novels ever. Although he was born a rich count, he often wore a plain peasant's blouse, as in this portrait.
photos.k: Why would a rich man wear peasant clothes?

photos.cr: Hershey Family Art Purchase Fund
photos.why: James Arthur made this picture as art, which was a radical idea in the 1890s. A young woman holds roses in soft light, like a painting.
photos.k: Why was it radical to call a photograph art?
photos.pr: Gelatin silver print mounted to glass

photos.why: Gertrude Käsebier photographed Clarence H. White Sr., a fellow photographer, in 1897. They were friends in the Photo-Secession and pushed for photography as art.
photos.k: What do you think the friends talked about?

photos.t: After the Massacre, Christian Quarter, Canea
photos.why: Underwood and Underwood photographed a ruined street in Canea, Crete, in 1897 after a conflict. The picture was sold as a stereograph to people at home.
photos.k: Why would people at home want to see this?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Detroit Publishing Company photographed Denver in 1897 with the snowy Rocky Mountains in the distance. The mountains stand tall behind a growing city.
photos.k: How does a city look with mountains behind it?

photos.cr: Hugh Edwards Photography and Media Purchase Fund
photos.why: Eugène Atget photographed the shops and streets of old Paris. This corner shop with its sign and displays is a small piece of vanished city life.
photos.k: What kinds of things do you think this shop sold?

photos.cr: Julien Levy Collection, Special Photography Acquisition Fund
photos.why: A street musician pushes his hand organ down a Paris lane. Atget made hundreds of pictures of street trades, for artists who wanted to record everyday Paris.
photos.k: What kind of music do you think he played?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed bare trees and a path by streetlights in a freezing night. It took long exposures and patience, and the soft glow makes the park look like a winter dream.
photos.k: What sounds would you hear in a park on a freezing night?

photos.t: Mount of the Holy Cross, Colorado
photos.why: William Henry Jackson photographed this peak, where snow fills the cracks in the shape of a cross. In the 1890s his company used a Swiss process called photochrom to add color to black-and-white photographs, and postcards like this were a sensation.
photos.k: Find the cross on the mountain.

photos.why: Geronimo was an Apache leader who fought for years to protect his people's homeland. At the time of this portrait, he was a prisoner of war and was taken to an exposition in Omaha, Nebraska, where he was photographed.
photos.k: What do you read in his face?

photos.cr: Gift of John Flory, Elizabeth Flory Kelly, and Phoebe Flory
photos.why: Clarence H. White photographed a row of telegraph poles in 1898. The poles stand like a rhythm of lines against the sky.
photos.k: Why are telegraph poles interesting to look at?

photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed New York City on an icy night in 1898. The glow of lamps and the icy sheen show how he loved bad weather.
photos.k: What would you wear on a night like this?

photos.why: Charles S. Harrington photographed the Columbus Avenue station of the Boston and Albany Railroad in 1898. The East end of the line had tracks lined with signals and cars.
photos.k: What does a station feel like when a train arrives?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Keystone View Company made a stereograph of Grant's Tomb in New York in the 1890s. The huge granite tomb honors General Ulysses S. Grant, the Civil War hero and 18th president.
photos.k: Why would a general have such a huge tomb?

photos.cr: Gift of Daniel, Richard, and Jonathan Logan
photos.why: Gertrude Käsebier posed a mother in white and her daughter in dark clothes in a doorway. The picture, named for a line from the Bible, made her famous when it was shown at galleries.
photos.k: Why do you think one is dressed in white and the other in black?

photos.cr: Gift of Mina Turner
photos.why: Käsebier's The Manger shows a mother and child bathed in soft light, like a modern Madonna. She believed photographers could make pictures as moving as paintings.
photos.k: How do the soft light and white dress change the mood?

photos.cr: Julien Levy Collection, Special Photography Acquisition Fund
photos.why: A woman carries a big basket of bread on a Paris street. Eugène Atget photographed street workers, and the pictures became a record of old Parisian jobs.
photos.k: What other jobs on the street do you know about?

photos.cr: Harold L. Stuart Endowment
photos.why: A man walks a Paris lane with lampshades piled on his arm. Atget photographed people who sold things on the street and sold his prints to artists, who used them as references.
photos.k: How many lampshades can you see?

photos.why: Nikola Tesla sits calmly while artificial lightning crackles from his giant coil in Colorado Springs. The photograph is a double exposure: he sat in one shot, and the sparks were added in another, since he would not have survived real lightning that close.
photos.k: Why do you think they used a double exposure?

photos.t: Columbia Glacier from Heather Island, Alaska
photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed the Columbia Glacier in Alaska in 1899 as part of the Harriman Alaska Expedition. He was the official photographer on the trip.
photos.k: How would you get to Alaska in 1899?

photos.why: Underwood and Underwood photographed Sixth Avenue in New York in 1899, when horse carts and elevated trains shared the street. The elevated railway ran above the avenue.
photos.k: What sounds would you hear?

photos.why: Frances Benjamin Johnston photographed schoolgirls doing exercises at the Hampton Institute in Virginia around 1899. She documented the school for the Paris Exposition.
photos.k: What exercises would you do?

photos.why: Frances Benjamin Johnston photographed two African American men and a cabin at the Hampton Institute in Virginia in 1899. She was one of the first women press photographers.
photos.k: What does the cabin tell you about the people?

photos.why: Clarence H. White made a triptych, a picture in three parts, called Spring in 1899. Women in white dresses stand in an orchard of blooming trees.
photos.k: How does a triptych tell a story?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Detroit Photographic Company photographed the Cliff House, a famous restaurant on a cliff above the Pacific in San Francisco, in 1899. Tourists loved to see the sea lions on the rocks below.
photos.k: Would you like to eat on a cliff above the sea?

photos.cr: Gift of Arielle Kozloff Brodkey in memory of Dr. Jerald S. Brodkey
photos.why: Frederick H. Evans photographed English cathedrals, waiting hours for the light to be just right. He printed on platinum paper, which gave soft, silvery grays, and refused to touch up his pictures.
photos.k: How does the light make the stone look?

photos.cr: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Frank Kolodny
photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed a huge circle of tipis on the prairie during a Piegan sun dance gathering. He spent thirty years documenting Native American communities.
photos.k: Why would so many families gather together on the prairie?
photos.pr: Photogravure, plate 192 from "The North American Indian, Volume 6" (1911)

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: James Craig Annan, a Scottish photographer, made soft, dark prints of the castle on its rock. He used a printing method called photogravure, which gave rich, velvet-like tones.
photos.k: How does the castle look against the sky?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: In a gentle snowstorm, horse-drawn carriages move along Fifth Avenue in New York. Stieglitz made the picture soft, like a painting, and printed it in a way that glowed.
photos.k: What is moving along the street? What isn't moving?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: A slim young tree stands on a wet New York street in a soft mist of rain. Stieglitz loved to photograph weather, and he used it to make the picture look like a drawing.
photos.k: Does it feel like a happy rain or a sad one?

photos.why: Gertrude Käsebier photographed members of Buffalo Bill's Wild West show when they came to New York. Amos Two Bulls, a Lakota man, is shown in a dignified profile, in a picture that looks like a painting.
photos.k: What do you think he is looking at?

photos.t: Tree in Snow, New York City
photos.cr: Gift of Flora Stieglitz Straus
photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed a tree in the snow in New York City around 1900. The tree stands like a drawing against the white.
photos.k: How does snow change the look of a tree?

photos.t: Eggs of a Stone-Curlew or Plover
photos.cr: John L. Severance Fund
photos.why: Richard Tepe photographed the eggs of a stone-curlew, a bird that nests on the ground. The speckled eggs are hard to see on the pebbles.
photos.k: Why are the eggs speckled?
photos.pr: silver print on printing out paper

photos.cr: Gift of Barbara Tannenbaum and Mark Soppeland
photos.why: An unknown photographer photographed Krishna's Butter Ball, a huge boulder balanced on a slope at Mahabalipuram in southern India. It looks as if it could roll, but it has stood still for over a thousand years.
photos.k: Why doesn't the giant rock roll away?
photos.pr: Gelatin silver print, toned, on collodion printing-out paper

photos.t: Crossing the Missouri River by Bridge
photos.why: Agnes Winterbottom Cooney photographed the crossing of the Missouri River in Nebraska around 1900. She was an amateur who documented family life on the Plains.
photos.k: How would you cross a big river?

photos.why: Gertrude Käsebier photographed Chief Flying Hawk of the Oglala Lakota in 1898. He was in Buffalo Bill's Wild West show, and Käsebier made dignified portraits of the performers.
photos.k: How does the portrait show respect?

photos.why: Gertrude Käsebier photographed Chief Iron Tail, a Lakota man who traveled with Buffalo Bill's Wild West show, in 1898. His portrait was one of her best known.
photos.k: What do you notice about his face?

photos.why: Underwood and Underwood photographed Bengal Lancers on parade as part of an event for a British prince. Their turbans and lances made them look grand.
photos.k: What do the lancers' uniforms look like?

photos.why: This is an autochrome, an early color photograph on glass, of the British photographer Olive Edis. Autochromes, which first appeared in 1907, used dyed starch grains to make color.
photos.k: How do you think starch grains make color?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Bain News Service photographed Truman Newberry, a Detroit businessman and later senator, and his wife. George Grantham Bain's news photo agency covered many famous people.
