photos.k: Why would a news agency photograph politicians?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Selma Lagerlöf was a Swedish writer who wrote The Wonderful Adventures of Nils. She became the first woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1909.
photos.k: Have you read any stories by Selma Lagerlöf?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Detroit Publishing Company photographed the Western Promenade, a hilltop park, in Portland, Maine, around 1900. Ladies in long dresses stroll along it.
photos.k: What would you do on a hilltop walk?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Detroit Publishing Company photographed Schenley Park in Pittsburgh around 1900. The park was a gift to the city and gave people green space in the smoky industrial town.
photos.k: Why would a smoky city want a park?

photos.cr: Gift of Mrs. Everett Kovler
photos.why: Eugène Atget photographed the park of Versailles in 1901 at dawn, when no one was around. He made hundreds of pictures of the empty gardens.
photos.k: Why would you photograph a garden at dawn?

photos.cr: Gift of Mrs. Everett Kovler
photos.why: Atget photographed a statue of the Rhône river god by Jean-Baptiste Tuby at Versailles in 1901. The reclining river god sits among the fountains.
photos.k: What does a river god look like?

photos.cr: Gift of Mrs. Everett Kovler
photos.why: Atget photographed a basin of water in the north gardens of Versailles in 1901. His pictures of fountains and statues were bought by artists.
photos.k: Why would artists buy photographs of gardens?

photos.t: When the Sands Are Running Low
photos.why: Gertrude Käsebier made this portrait in 1901. A woman and a girl look at an hourglass, and the picture is about passing time.
photos.k: What does the hourglass mean?

photos.why: Gertrude Käsebier photographed Frederick H. Evans, the English photographer of cathedrals, in 1901. Käsebier met many photographers in London.
photos.k: Why would one photographer photograph another?

photos.why: The Boston Elevated Railway photographed the south end of a platform at Boylston Station in June 1901. The subway, started in 1897, was the first in America.
photos.k: What was it like to ride the first subway?

photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed his daughter Kitty in Central Park, New York, in 1901. Fathers were often the best photographers of their families.
photos.k: Why would a father take lots of pictures of his daughter?

photos.why: Gertrude Käsebier photographed a Native American man in Wild West show costume in 1901. Her pictures were dignified portraits of people who were often treated as curiosities.
photos.k: How do you want to look in a portrait?

photos.why: Alfonso XIII was king of Spain from the day he was born in 1886 until 1931. This portrait by Underwood and Underwood was made when he was still a teenager.
photos.k: What would it be like to be a king from birth?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Detroit Photographic Company photographed Lead, a gold mining town in the Black Hills of South Dakota, around 1901. The Homestake Mine, the biggest gold mine in America, was there.
photos.k: What would life in a mining town be like?

photos.why: Edward Steichen photographed the sculptor Auguste Rodin in front of his famous statue The Thinker. In the dark, Rodin's shadow seems to join the statue.
photos.k: Which one is the sculpture and which is the sculptor?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: A steam locomotive moves out of a rail yard in New York in smoky light. Stieglitz showed that machines and cities could be as beautiful as landscapes.
photos.k: What do you hear when a train passes?

photos.why: Gertrude Käsebier photographed her friend and fellow photographer Alfred Stieglitz in 1902, the year he founded the Photo-Secession, a group that fought to make photography respected as an art.
photos.k: What does his face say about a man who was determined?

photos.cr: Gift of John Flory, Elizabeth Flory Kelly, and Phoebe Flory
photos.why: Clarence H. White photographed a woman holding a peacock feather in 1902. His soft poses and light make it look like a painting.
photos.k: What does a peacock feather look like?
photos.pr: platinum print with crayon and gouache

photos.cr: Gift of Michael Mattis and Judith Hochberg
photos.why: Frédéric Boissonnas photographed the Parthenon in Athens in 1902. The temple was built for the goddess Athena in the 400s BC.
photos.k: How have the columns survived for so long?

photos.why: Gertrude Käsebier made this dignified portrait of Bears One, a Dakota Sioux man, in 1902. She photographed performers from Buffalo Bill's show in her New York studio.
photos.k: What do you see in his expression?

photos.why: William Henry Jackson photographed a hunting dog standing still in profile, around 1902. A pointer holds this pose when it finds game.
photos.k: How does a dog know to freeze like that?

photos.t: Rice Fields and Tea Bushes, South China
photos.why: Underwood and Underwood photographed terraced rice fields and tea bushes in southern China about 1902. They sold 3D stereographs of the world to people who stayed at home.
photos.k: What do you think farming rice on steps is like?

photos.t: Sunday Afternoon, Golden Gate Park, San Francisco
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A crowd enjoys a Sunday afternoon in Golden Gate Park in San Francisco in 1902. Ladies and gentlemen in their best clothes stroll the paths.
photos.k: What would you do in a park on a Sunday in 1902?

photos.t: The Sweetest Spot on Earth: Sugar Levee, New Orleans
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Underwood and Underwood photographed barrels and sacks of sugar piled along the levee in New Orleans around 1902. The port shipped sugar from Louisiana plantations.
photos.k: How would you move so many sacks?

photos.cr: Purchased with funds provided by Mr. and Mrs. Gaylord Donnelley
photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed the adobe houses of Zuni Pueblo in New Mexico, stacked like steps with ladders to the upper levels. The pueblo has been lived in for hundreds of years.
photos.k: How would you get up to the top floor?
photos.pr: Photogravure on vellum, from "The North American Indian"

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Stieglitz photographed the new Flatiron Building in a snowfall, its triangular shape rising behind a bare tree. He said it looked like the bow of a ship moving toward him.
photos.k: Do you see why people compared the building to a ship?

photos.why: Chief Joseph, a Nez Perce leader, led his people on a long, desperate journey in 1877 to avoid being forced onto a reservation. Edward Curtis photographed him in 1903, the year before he died.
photos.k: What do you think he is thinking about?

photos.why: On December 17, 1903, at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, Orville Wright flew the first powered airplane for twelve seconds and 120 feet. A man named John Daniels pressed the shutter of a camera aimed at the plane just as it left the ground, while Wilbur ran alongside.
photos.k: Find the person running at the right. Who do you think it is?

photos.why: Clarence H. White photographed a boy reading Camera Work, the magazine of art photography published by Alfred Stieglitz, in 1903. It shows how the new photography world spread through magazines.
photos.k: Why would a magazine matter to a boy?

photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed an Apache woman with her baby on a cradleboard, around 1903. Curtis spent thirty years photographing Native American peoples for his twenty-volume work The North American Indian.
photos.k: How does a cradleboard help carry a baby?

photos.why: Gertrude Käsebier photographed Adolf de Meyer, a photographer known for dreamy fashion pictures, in 1903. De Meyer later became the first fashion photographer.
photos.k: What is fashion photography?

photos.why: William Henry Jackson, famous for his pictures of the West, made this portrait of a woman named Editha in 1903. He ran a photography business in Denver.
photos.k: Why would a landscape photographer make portraits?

photos.t: Ely Cathedral: A Memory of the Past
photos.why: Frederick H. Evans photographed Ely Cathedral in England for Camera Work in 1903. He never touched up his prints and always waited for the best light.
photos.k: Why would a photographer wait for the right light?

photos.t: Height and Light in Bourges Cathedral
photos.why: Frederick H. Evans photographed the soaring interior of Bourges Cathedral in France. His pictures of cathedrals lead the eye upward in rich, quiet light.
photos.k: How does the picture make you look up?

photos.why: The U.S. Army Engineer Office photographed the Seventh Street Bridge in Pittsburgh around 1903. Bridges crossed the three rivers of Pittsburgh.
photos.k: Why would a city need many bridges?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed the home of the Havasupai people, who lived in a canyon off the Grand Canyon in Arizona. The small dwellings sit beneath tall red cliffs.
photos.k: What would life at the bottom of a canyon be like?

photos.t: President Roosevelt Dedicating the Fort Fisher Monument in the Rain
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: William Herman Rau photographed Theodore Roosevelt finishing a speech in the rain at a memorial in 1903. Crowds held umbrellas while the president spoke.
photos.k: Would you stay to hear a speech in the rain?

photos.cr: Acquired through exchange with George Eastman House
photos.why: Lewis Hine photographed an immigrant mother and her children at Ellis Island. Hine named it after paintings of Mary and the baby Jesus, to show that these families deserved respect.
photos.k: What do you think this mother hopes for her children?

photos.why: Edward Steichen made this picture of a moonlit pond in New York by printing it in layers of green and blue pigment. It was one of the first photographs to sell for a high price.
photos.k: Can you find the reflections of the trees?

photos.t: Laborers at Work on the Panama Canal
photos.why: In 1904 the United States began building a canal across Panama to link the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. Thousands of workers, many from the Caribbean, dug through mountains in the hot sun.
photos.k: What tools do you think they used?

photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed Navajo riders walking across the floor of a canyon in Arizona, tiny compared with the tall red cliffs. The picture is one of his most famous.
photos.k: How tall do you think the cliffs are compared with the riders?

photos.why: Richard Strauss was a German composer who wrote the music that opens the film 2001: A Space Odyssey. Edward Steichen photographed him in dramatic shadow.
photos.k: What kind of music do you think he would write?

photos.why: Steichen photographed the Flatiron Building in rainy twilight, and printed it in blue-green tones with a few touches of color. The picture feels like a painting of a misty New York evening.
photos.k: What time of day does it feel like?

photos.cr: Gift of Mrs. Everett Kovler
photos.why: Eugène Atget photographed a statue at Versailles by Girardon showing the god Pluto carrying off Proserpina. He photographed the statues of the park in all seasons.
photos.k: What story does the statue tell?

photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed the arrival of a ship in 1904. He loved the moment of approaching land, and the picture shows passengers and a shoreline in soft haze.
photos.k: What does it feel like to see land after a long journey?

photos.why: Alvin Langdon Coburn photographed the playwright George Bernard Shaw in 1904. Shaw was a friend and a big fan of photography.
photos.k: What does a famous playwright look like?

photos.t: Russian Soldiers in a Sorghum Field
photos.why: Sergei Prokudin-Gorsky photographed Russian soldiers in a tall sorghum field in Manchuria during the Russo-Japanese War in 1904. The tall crop provided cover for an ambush.
photos.k: Why would soldiers hide in a field?

photos.why: The U.S. Army medical museum photographed an operating room in a hospital in Hiroshima during the Russo-Japanese War in 1904. Doctors and nurses cared for wounded soldiers.
photos.k: How do you think surgery differed in 1904?

photos.why: Edward Steichen photographed a pond at Mamaroneck, New York, at night in 1904. He printed it in layers of colored gum so that moonlight glows through the trees.
photos.k: How can a photograph glow like moonlight?

photos.t: Opening Day Crowd at the Louisiana Purchase Exposition
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A huge crowd gathers around a column on opening day at the 1904 World's Fair in St. Louis. The fair celebrated the 100th anniversary of the Louisiana Purchase.
photos.k: How would you celebrate such an anniversary?

photos.t: Grand Plaza at the Louisiana Purchase Exposition
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: William Herman Rau photographed the Grand Plaza at the 1904 fair in St. Louis. The fair buildings were huge and white, with fountains and flags.
photos.k: How many buildings can you see?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Schoolchildren gather at the base of the Louisiana Monument at the 1904 St. Louis World's Fair. The fair welcomed many school groups.
photos.k: What would you want to see at a world's fair?

photos.t: Louisiana Purchase Monument and Palace of Varied Industries
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Keystone View Company made a stereograph of the monument and one of the biggest buildings at the 1904 fair. The Palace of Varied Industries was full of products.
photos.k: What kinds of products would the palace display?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Detroit Publishing Company photographed Havana, Cuba, in 1904. The panorama shows the city of the harbor with its low colorful buildings.
photos.k: What do you notice about the buildings?

photos.cr: Acquired through exchange with George Eastman House
photos.why: A boy in a cap breaks into a big grin. Lewis Hine photographed working children across the US, and often caught their personalities as well as their hard lives.
photos.k: What do you think made him smile?

photos.cr: Acquired through exchange with George Eastman House
photos.why: On a hot New York day, a baby sleeps on a cushion outside while an old man rests by the wall of a tenement. Crowded apartments were so stuffy that families took their children out into the street.
photos.k: Where do you like to go when it's too hot at home?

photos.cr: Gift of David Vestal
photos.why: Lewis Hine photographed new arrivals at Ellis Island, where about twelve million immigrants entered the United States. This young woman wears a headscarf and an open, serious expression.
photos.k: What do you think she hoped to find in America?

photos.cr: The Mary and Leigh Block Endowment Fund
photos.why: A family sits together on a bench in the great hall at Ellis Island, waiting to learn whether they can enter the country. Hine treated each family as individuals.
photos.k: What would you pack if you were moving to another country?

photos.cr: Gift of David Vestal
photos.why: A family stands near piles of luggage at Ellis Island, looking for their lost bags. Hine's pictures show that arriving in a new country was hard.
photos.k: What would be the first thing you'd look for?

photos.why: The French sculptor Auguste Rodin made The Thinker and many other famous statues. Gertrude Käsebier photographed him in Paris with his white beard glowing against a pale background.
photos.k: What kind of things would a sculptor see in a block of stone?

photos.why: H. G. Wells wrote science fiction classics such as The Time Machine and The War of the Worlds. Alvin Langdon Coburn photographed him with his chin resting on his hand, as if thinking about the future.
photos.k: What would you invent if you could travel in time?

photos.cr: Gift of Mrs. Everett Kovler
photos.why: Eugène Atget photographed a stone vase in the park at Versailles in 1905. Atget's carefully framed pictures of statues and vases were used by artists as models.
photos.k: Why would a vase make a good subject?

photos.cr: Gift of Michael F. Resch
photos.why: The Foto Imperio studio in Mexico was run by Andrés and Francisco Hernández. They made portraits of families and soldiers for decades.
photos.k: How does a studio portrait show the person?

photos.why: Sergei Prokudin-Gorsky photographed poppies in color around 1905 using three filters. It is one of the earliest color pictures of flowers.
photos.k: How did he make a color picture before color film?

photos.why: Lewis Hine photographed a man with an amputated arm at Ellis Island around 1905. Hine took the picture for the Ethical Culture Society to show the dignity of immigrants.
photos.k: What do you think the man's story is?

photos.why: Sergei Prokudin-Gorsky photographed the town of Lugano in Switzerland in about 1905 in early color. The lake and mountains shine in three-color blends.
photos.k: What colors do you see in the lake?

photos.t: Immigrant Family in the Baggage Room at Ellis Island
photos.why: Lewis Hine photographed an immigrant family waiting in the baggage room at Ellis Island in New York around 1905. Millions of immigrants entered the United States through Ellis Island.
photos.k: What would you do if you arrived in a new country?

photos.why: Gertrude Käsebier photographed Frances Benjamin Johnston in 1905. Both were pioneering women photographers.
photos.k: Why would two women photographers admire each other?

photos.why: Sergei Prokudin-Gorsky photographed a long-legged buzzard, a bird of prey, in the Hungry Steppe of Central Asia. Early color pictures of wildlife are rare.
photos.k: How does a bird of prey look at you?

photos.why: Sergei Prokudin-Gorsky photographed Italian women in color in 1905 during his trip to Europe. He made three exposures through colored filters.
photos.k: How do three black-and-white pictures make one in color?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed a Navajo farm in 1905. Fields of corn and a small hogan sit in a high desert.
photos.k: How would you grow corn in a dry place?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Underwood and Underwood photographed Theodore Roosevelt giving a speech in 1905. Roosevelt was a big speaker with a strong voice and a famous pair of glasses.
photos.k: What do speeches do for a crowd?

photos.cr: Gift of David Vestal
photos.why: A group of newsboys stand in the shadow of the Brooklyn Bridge with stacks of newspapers. Hine's pictures showed that many boys worked long hours selling papers in city streets.
photos.k: What time of day do you think they started work?

photos.why: On April 18, 1906, a huge earthquake and the fires that followed destroyed much of San Francisco and killed about three thousand people. This view of the ruins shows block after block flattened.
photos.k: What would it be like to see your city like this?

photos.cr: Gift of Mrs. Everett Kovler
photos.why: Eugène Atget photographed the park at Versailles in 1906. Empty paths run between clipped trees and statues in the dim light of early morning.
photos.k: What would it be like to be alone in this park?

photos.cr: Gift of John Flory, Elizabeth Flory Kelly, and Phoebe Flory
photos.why: Clarence H. White photographed women resting in a garden arbor in 1906. His soft light and quiet poses make everyday moments look like paintings.
photos.k: What do you do in a garden?

photos.why: This photograph, published in Camera Work in July 1906, shows a city street after a big snowstorm. Photographers of that era loved snow and rain.
photos.k: What changes in a city after a blizzard?

photos.why: Arnold Genthe photographed the author Jack London in 1906. London wrote The Call of the Wild and White Fang.
photos.k: Have you read any Jack London stories?

photos.why: Arnold Genthe photographed a girl called Little Plum Blossom in San Francisco's Chinatown around 1906. His pictures of the neighborhood are some of the only records before the earthquake.
photos.k: What do you think she was like?

photos.why: This portrait in Camera Work in April 1906 shows the American painter William Merritt Chase. Photographers loved to portray famous artists.
photos.k: What does a painter's studio feel like?

photos.why: Genthe photographed his bungalow in Carmel, California, around 1906, where he hosted writers and artists. The cottage was in the pine trees.
photos.k: Would you like to live in a cabin among pines?

photos.t: Midnight at the Bowery Mission Bread Line
photos.why: Lewis Hine photographed men waiting for bread at the Bowery Mission in New York at midnight in 1906. The mission fed the poor, and Hine took pictures to show the need.
photos.k: Why would people line up at midnight?

photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed Alchise, a Chiricahua Apache man, around 1906. Alchise was a scout for the army and a leader.
photos.k: What can a face tell you?

photos.why: Edward Steichen was one of the first artists to try Autochrome, the first practical color process. Women in light summer dresses lounge on a veranda, and the soft colors look like an Impressionist painting.
photos.k: What colors do you notice? How does it feel to see old photographs in color?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: A girl holds a bowl of fruit in this color photograph. The Lumière brothers began selling Autochrome plates in 1907. They used tiny dyed grains of potato starch as color filters, and Stieglitz was one of the first artists to try them on his daughter Kitty.
photos.k: How are the colors different from the colors in a modern photo?

photos.cr: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Frank Kolodny
photos.why: Hollow Horn Bear was a Lakota leader who served as a scout and a chief. Edward Curtis photographed him in 1907, and his face later appeared on a US postage stamp.
photos.k: What can you tell about him from his face?
photos.pr: Photogravure, plate 82 from "The North American Indian, Volume 3" (1908)

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: On a ship crossing to Europe, Alfred Stieglitz looked down from the first-class deck at passengers in the cheaper steerage section. He rushed to get his camera and had one plate left. The shapes of the gangway, funnel and straw hat make a picture that helped begin modern photography.
photos.k: Find the straight lines and the round shapes. How do they fit together?

photos.t: Frank Eugene Seated at a Table
photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz made some of the first color photographs in America with Autochrome plates. Here his friend Frank Eugene, a photographer and painter, sits at a table with flowers and glasses.
photos.k: Do the soft colors feel like a painting?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: A girl in a straw hat and striped dress leans sideways in the sun in this Autochrome by Stieglitz. The glowing pink and blue come from tiny grains of colored starch.
photos.k: How is it different from a black-and-white portrait?

photos.why: Alvin Langdon Coburn made an autochrome portrait of George Bernard Shaw in 1907. Autochromes were the first practical color photographs.
photos.k: How does early color look different from today's?

photos.t: The Novels and Tales of Henry James, Volume 1
photos.why: Alvin Langdon Coburn made a series of photographs for the 1907 New York edition of Henry James's novels. Each volume had a frontispiece of a place from the story.
photos.k: Why would a book need a photograph?

photos.why: An unknown photographer captured a kingfisher on a branch in 1907, slightly blurred by movement. Birds were hard to photograph in the days of slow lenses.
photos.k: What would make a bird blur in a photograph?

photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed a group of Apache baskets for his book The North American Indian. Their patterns are woven with great skill.
photos.k: What patterns do you see in the baskets?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Theodore Roosevelt speaks to a crowd in Indianapolis, Indiana, in 1907. Presidents often took trains around the country to give speeches.
photos.k: How did the president reach the crowd without a microphone?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: This photograph shows the tomb of Andrew Jackson in the garden of the Hermitage, his home near Nashville, Tennessee, in 1907. Jackson was the seventh president.
photos.k: Why do people visit presidents' homes?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Detroit Publishing Company made a six-part panorama of Minneapolis in 1907. The city sits on the Mississippi River at St. Anthony Falls, which powered its flour mills.
photos.k: How could a river power a mill?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed a Pima home in Arizona in 1907. The home is a round house made of brush and mud.
photos.k: What materials would you use to build a desert home?

photos.why: Lewis Hine photographed children working in cotton mills across the American South. This tiny girl stands among the huge spinning machines. His pictures helped convince Americans to pass laws against child labor.
photos.k: How old do you think she is? How would you feel working in this mill?

photos.cr: Acquired through exchange with George Eastman House
photos.why: Sadie Pfeifer, a young girl, stands at a spinning frame in a South Carolina cotton mill. Lewis Hine compared children's heights with his coat buttons to estimate how old they were. His photographs helped end child labor.
photos.k: How would you feel working in a mill instead of going to school?

photos.cr: Gift of David Vestal
photos.why: In coal mines, trapper boys sat alone in the dark and opened and closed doors to let cars through. They sometimes worked ten hours a day. Hine photographed boys like this one in West Virginia.
photos.k: How would you spend ten hours in the dark?

photos.why: Sergey Prokudin-Gorsky took this color portrait of the famous writer Leo Tolstoy sitting in a garden at his estate in 1908. It is one of the first color photographs of a major writer.
photos.k: What does it feel like to see someone from over a century ago in color?

photos.why: Mark Twain, the author of Tom Sawyer, liked to write in bed. This Autochrome shows him in a red robe, reading with white hair against the pillow.
photos.k: What book would you read in bed?

photos.why: Boys who worked in an Indiana glassworks pose in front of the factory. Lewis Hine photographed child workers and kept notes of their names and ages, hoping to show that laws were needed.
photos.k: How old do you think the youngest boy is?

photos.why: Boys work through the night in a glass factory, where a furnace glows in the dark. Hine sometimes sneaked into factories pretending to be a salesman, so he could photograph the working children.
photos.k: Why do you think the boys worked at night?

photos.why: Alvin Langdon Coburn photographed the tall rigging of a ship reflected in the water so it forms a web of lines. He wanted pictures to be as beautiful as paintings and prints.
photos.k: Can you find the ship's masts and their reflections?

photos.t: Still Life, Autochrome by Baron de Meyer
photos.why: Adolph de Meyer made an autochrome still life in 1908, with flowers and fruit in soft color. Autochromes were made with dyed potato starch.
photos.k: What colors do you see in the fruit?

photos.why: Alvin Langdon Coburn photographed George Bernard Shaw in 1908 for a book. Shaw posed as Rodin's The Thinker, and the picture is famous.
photos.k: What would you pose as for a funny photograph?

photos.why: Edward Steichen photographed himself around 1902 with a palette and brush. He was both a painter and a photographer.
photos.k: Why would a photographer pose as a painter?

photos.why: Herbert Ponting photographed Mount Fuji in Japan in about 1908. Ponting traveled the world before becoming the photographer on Scott's Antarctic expedition.
photos.k: Why would people think a mountain is sacred?

photos.why: Alvin Langdon Coburn made an autochrome of a woman in a blue dress in 1908. The dye grains give it a soft glow.
photos.k: How does the blue dress shine in the picture?

photos.why: Alvin Langdon Coburn photographed William De Morgan, a potter and novelist, on July 21, 1908. Coburn made portraits of famous men for a book.
photos.k: How can a person be both a potter and a novelist?

photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed a burial platform of the Apsáalooke, or Crow, people in 1908. Their traditions placed the dead on high platforms.
photos.k: Why do cultures have different ways of caring for the dead?

photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed Bear's Belly, a member of the Arikara medicine society, wrapped in a bear skin in 1908. His pictures preserved ceremonies.
photos.k: Why would a person wear a bear skin?

photos.t: Mill Workers in Cherryville, North Carolina
photos.why: Lewis Hine photographed young mill workers at the Cherryville Manufacturing Company in North Carolina in 1908. Children worked long hours in mills.
photos.k: How would you feel working in a mill at ten years old?

photos.t: President Theodore Roosevelt with Members of the U.S. Team
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: President Theodore Roosevelt stands with American athletes in 1908. The 1908 Olympics were held in London.
photos.k: What sport would you like to try in the Olympics?

photos.t: Blue Earth, Minnesota: A Busy Day
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The photograph shows a busy day on the main street of Blue Earth, Minnesota, in 1908. Horses, wagons and people crowd the street.
photos.k: What do you see on a busy small-town street?

photos.cr: Acquired through exchange with George Eastman House
photos.why: A girl holds a baby on her hip. In many poor families, older children took care of their little brothers and sisters while the grown-ups worked. Lewis Hine photographed families in Pittsburgh for a big study of working-class life.
photos.k: Do you help care for younger children?

photos.cr: Gift of David Vestal
photos.why: Three coal miners with lamps on their caps stand together. Hine photographed men who had spent decades underground in Pennsylvania, so people above ground could see who dug the coal.
photos.k: What would it feel like to work in the dark every day?

photos.cr: Gift of David Vestal
photos.why: A Welsh coal miner looks upward with the lamp on his cap shining. Hine called the picture "Follow the Gleam," because a miner's lamp was his only light underground.
photos.k: Where do you think his lamp is shining?

photos.why: Sergei Prokudin-Gorsky photographed Monk Makarii at his cell in 1909. The photograph was made with three exposures through colored filters, so we can see his black robe against green.
photos.k: What colors do you see?

photos.why: Lewis Hine photographed newsboys in the streets in 1909, working long hours for pennies. His pictures helped campaign against child labor.
photos.k: Why would a ten-year-old be selling newspapers?

photos.t: Amateur Football on the Boston Common
photos.why: Lewis Hine photographed boys playing football on the Boston Common in 1909. Even for Hine, who photographed work, play was a good subject.
photos.k: What would football look like without helmets?

photos.why: Alvin Langdon Coburn made photographs for Henry James's novel The Golden Bowl in 1909. The frontispiece showed a London shop window.
photos.k: How can a photograph illustrate a story?

photos.why: George Grantham Bain photographed a crowded dormitory in a lodging house, probably in Boston, in 1909. Rows of beds hold men who have no home.
photos.k: Why would the city provide this?

photos.why: Sergey Prokudin-Gorsky took three black-and-white pictures of the same scene through red, green and blue filters, and combined them into a color image. This field of poppies is one of his early color experiments.
photos.k: How do the three filters help show true colors?

photos.why: Prokudin-Gorsky traveled to Switzerland and photographed a mountain lake in color. Few people had ever seen real color photographs like this, a century ago.
photos.k: What colors surprise you most?

photos.why: A vase of white flowers sits on a bright red tablecloth. Prokudin-Gorsky used still lifes to test his color process, since a still life does not move between the three exposures.
photos.k: Why is a still life easier for his method than a street scene?

photos.t: Newsies at Skeeter Branch, St. Louis
photos.cr: Purchased with funds provided by Charles and Ruth Levy Foundation
photos.why: Boys sell newspapers on a city street. Some of these newsboys were only ten or eleven years old and had already learned grown-up habits. Hine hoped his pictures would show how hard these children's lives were.
photos.k: What would you do if you were a newsboy?

photos.t: On the Shore of the Lake, Kutenai
photos.cr: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Frank Kolodny
photos.why: A Kutenai person stands beside a canoe with an unusual pointed shape, called a sturgeon-nose canoe, on a lake shore. Edward Curtis photographed many peoples of the Pacific Northwest.
photos.k: What do you notice about the shape of the canoe?
photos.pr: Photogravure, plate 251 from "The North American Indian, Volume 7" (1911)

photos.why: Sergey Prokudin-Gorsky photographed a sunny path through a tall pine forest in color. The trees glow gold and green, much as they would for someone standing there more than a hundred years ago.
photos.k: What would it smell like in this forest?

photos.why: Addie Card was twelve years old when Lewis Hine photographed her at a cotton mill in North Pownal, Vermont. She stands barefoot beside the spinning frames, looking right at the camera. Her face became a symbol of the fight against child labor.
photos.k: What do you think she was thinking when she looked at the camera?

photos.why: Green domes of a Russian church rise above a town on a river in this color photograph by Prokudin-Gorsky. He traveled across the Russian Empire for years, photographing it in color for the tsar.
photos.k: Why do you think he chose to photograph a church?

photos.why: Johan Beck made this color picture of Stockholm's royal palace at twilight, with a boat gliding past. Color photographs were brand new, and the soft hues give the scene a dreamy look.
photos.k: What time of day do you think it is?

photos.why: Tadeusz Rząca photographed the red-brick Collegium Novum, a building of Poland's Jagiellonian University, in color. He used Autochrome, the first practical color process.
photos.k: How many arches can you find?

photos.t: Profile Study of a Young Woman
photos.why: Gertrude Käsebier photographed a young woman in profile around 1910. Her use of soft light made the face glow.
photos.k: How does light change a face?

photos.why: Käsebier photographed a woman playing solitaire, a card game for one, around 1910. It may be a self-portrait.
photos.k: Why would someone play a game alone?

photos.t: Woman and Child by a River
photos.why: Gertrude Käsebier photographed a mother and child by a river around 1910. Käsebier was known for tender pictures of mothers and children.
photos.k: Why do mothers and children make good subjects?

photos.why: Eugène Atget photographed a wine merchant's shop on Rue Boyer in Paris around 1910. He recorded small shops and trades.
photos.k: What would you buy in a shop like this?

photos.why: Gertrude Käsebier photographed William Ivins, who would become the first curator of prints at the Metropolitan Museum of Art. The portrait was taken around 1910.
photos.k: What does a museum curator do?

photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed a Piegan man named Big Mouth Spring around 1910. The portrait is three-quarter length.
photos.k: What do you see in his face?

photos.why: Gertrude Käsebier photographed Mrs. Augustine Strickland around 1910 on platinum paper. Platinum prints have a soft, rich tone.
photos.k: What does the platinum print's softness do?

photos.why: Käsebier photographed a family in Woburn, Massachusetts, around 1910. Her family portraits seem relaxed and warm.
photos.k: How can a photographer make a family comfortable?

photos.t: Mother and Children with a Horse
photos.why: Käsebier photographed a mother with her children and a horse around 1910. The horse adds a gentle, rural feel.
photos.k: Why would a family pose with a horse?

photos.why: This photograph shows the Terra Nova, the ship that took Captain Robert Scott's expedition to Antarctica in 1910. The expedition would reach the South Pole in 1912 but all the men who made it would die on the way back.
photos.k: Why did explorers want to reach the South Pole?

photos.why: Eugène Atget photographed a fried food shop on Rue Mouffetard in Paris around 1910. Atget recorded old Paris trades before they disappeared.
photos.k: What smells would you notice in the street?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Detroit Publishing Company photographed Independence Square in Philadelphia around 1910. Independence Hall behind the square is where the Declaration of Independence was signed.
photos.k: Why is this place important in American history?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Detroit Publishing Company photographed the skyline and harbor of Baltimore, Maryland, around 1910. Ships crowd the waterfront.
photos.k: What kinds of boats do you see?

photos.t: Panorama of Madison Square, New York
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A nine-part panorama shows Madison Square in New York about 1910, with the Flatiron Building and the Metropolitan Life Tower. Crowds and carriages fill the park.
photos.k: How many tall buildings can you count?

photos.t: New Orleans and the Mississippi River
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A panorama of New Orleans and the Mississippi River from Algiers, made by the Detroit Publishing Company around 1910. Ships and steamers line the bend of the river.
photos.k: What do you notice about the shape of the river?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Detroit Publishing Company photographed the Detroit waterfront around 1910. Freighters and ferries moved on the Detroit River.
photos.k: Why would the photograph company be named after the city?

photos.t: Crowd Waiting to Go Up the Washington Monument
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A crowd waits to ride to the top of the Washington Monument in Washington, D.C., around 1910. Visitors have long loved the view from the top.
photos.k: How would you feel on top of a 555-foot tower?

photos.t: Offering the Pipe to the Earth, Cheyenne
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed a Cheyenne ceremony in Montana in 1910, where a man offers a pipe to the earth. Curtis recorded rituals as people feared they would be lost.
photos.k: Why does a ceremony honor the earth?

photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed Piegan, or Blackfeet, people at the water's edge around 1910. Their tipis stand beside the river under tall trees.
photos.k: What would a camp by a river sound like?

photos.t: Dancing to Restore an Eclipsed Moon
photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed a Hupa dance to restore an eclipsed moon around 1910. Many cultures have stories to explain an eclipse and ceremonies to bring the Moon back.
photos.k: What does your family say about an eclipse?

photos.cr: Gift of David Vestal
photos.why: Dozens of boys stand in front of a Pennsylvania coal breaker, where they picked slate from moving coal for hours. The sharp coal cut their fingers. Hine's photographs were used to push for laws against child labor.
photos.k: How many boys can you count?

photos.why: Sergey Prokudin-Gorsky photographed Alim Khan, the emir of Bukhara, in a bright blue robe covered in medals. The vivid color shows how bold the clothing of Central Asia was.
photos.k: What colors stand out? How do you think they looked in life?

photos.why: Harriet Tubman escaped slavery and then returned many times to lead others to freedom along the Underground Railroad. In this photograph she is an elderly woman in a white dress, near the end of her long life.
photos.k: What do you admire most about someone who risked her life for others?

photos.t: Wreck of the Gratitude, Macquarie Island
photos.why: Frank Hurley was the photographer on Douglas Mawson's expedition to Antarctica in 1911. On the way he photographed the wreck of the ship Gratitude and hundreds of penguins on Macquarie Island, a stop between Australia and the ice.
photos.k: How many penguins can you count?

photos.why: Herbert Ponting was the photographer on Captain Scott's Terra Nova expedition to Antarctica. He photographed a member of the team standing in a blue ice cave in an iceberg. Ponting was the first professional photographer to work in Antarctica.
photos.k: How cold do you think it was inside the ice?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed two towers in New York in 1911. He photographed the new skyscrapers with an eye for shapes and light.
photos.k: How do the two towers look different?

photos.why: Herbert Ponting photographed a grotto, a cave in an iceberg, during Captain Scott's British Antarctic Expedition in 1911. It is one of the famous pictures of the trip.
photos.k: How would the light look inside an ice cave?

photos.why: Sergei Prokudin-Gorsky photographed Alim Khan, the last emir of Bukhara, in 1911 in color. The emir wears a robe stitched with gold.
photos.k: How does color change a portrait?

photos.why: Herbert Ponting photographed a cavern in an iceberg in Antarctica in 1911. A person stands in the cave mouth to show how large it is.
photos.k: How do people show the scale of a giant ice cave?

photos.why: This advert for Tabloid Rytol shows Herbert Ponting developing film in Antarctica. His darkroom was in a hut at the edge of the sea ice.
photos.k: How would you develop film in the cold?

photos.t: Exterior of the Grotto Iceberg, Antarctica
photos.why: Herbert Ponting photographed the outside of an iceberg with a grotto during Captain Scott's expedition in 1911. The ice shines blue and white.
photos.k: What shapes does the ice make?

photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed a woman of the Nespelem people in 1911. His pictures show costumes and faces of the Pacific Northwest.
photos.k: What do her clothes tell you?

photos.why: Another picture by Herbert Ponting of a cave in an iceberg shows the arch of ice and the sea beneath. The Antarctic expedition members called it the grotto.
photos.k: Why does ice look blue?

photos.t: Skyline from the Lake Front, Chicago
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Detroit Publishing Company photographed Chicago's skyline from the lake front in 1911. Tall buildings rise beyond a park.
photos.k: What changed when skyscrapers were invented?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: In July 1911, Union and Confederate veterans met at Manassas, Virginia, for a Peace Jubilee on the 50th anniversary of the first Battle of Bull Run. President Taft spoke to the old soldiers.
photos.k: Why would former enemies meet 50 years later?

photos.why: A baby sleeps in a mother's arms in this early color photograph by the British amateur Henry Essenhigh Corke. The warm reds and browns come from the tiny dyed grains in an Autochrome plate.
photos.k: What would it feel like to hold a sleeping baby?

photos.t: A Log Cabin in the Forest
photos.why: Prokudin-Gorsky photographed a small log hut in a green clearing in Russia in color. The grass and trees look as bright and fresh as they would in a modern snapshot.
photos.k: Who might live in a hut like this?

photos.why: The Titanic, the largest ship in the world, left Southampton, England, on April 10, 1912, on her first voyage. She sank four days later after hitting an iceberg, and about 1,500 people lost their lives.
photos.k: How do you think the people on shore felt as she left?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed the painter Arthur Dove in 1912. Dove was one of the first American painters to make abstract art.
photos.k: What is abstract art?

photos.why: Lewis Hine photographed housing for workers at the Cannon Mills in Concord, North Carolina, in 1912. Company houses were crowded together near the mill.
photos.k: Why would workers live near the mill?

photos.why: This Antarctic scene from the Australasian Antarctic Expedition of 1911 to 1914 shows blue ice and seals. The name Venice comes from the water around the ice.
photos.k: Why would explorers call it a Venice?

photos.t: Interior of J. P. Morgan's Library
photos.why: Arnold Genthe photographed the library of the banker J. P. Morgan in New York around 1912. Shelves of rare books rise to the ceiling.
photos.k: What books would you keep in a big library?

photos.t: Boy Carrying Hats, Bleecker Street, New York
photos.why: Lewis Hine photographed a boy carrying piles of hats on Bleecker Street in New York in 1912. Children did piecework at home or in shops.
photos.k: Why would a child carry so many hats?

photos.t: A Radiant Turret Lit by the Midsummer Midnight Sun
photos.why: This photograph from the Australasian Antarctic Expedition shows an ice tower glowing in the midnight sun. In the Antarctic summer the sun never sets, and the ice turns gold and pink.
photos.k: What would it be like if the sun never set?

photos.t: Olympic Athletes' Parade on Fifth Avenue, 1912
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: American athletes parade up New York's Fifth Avenue in August 1912 after returning from the Stockholm Olympics. Crowds lined the street to cheer.
photos.k: How would you welcome home a champion?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A postcard-style photograph of mountain laurel in bloom at Woodstock, New York, in 1912. The pink and white flowers cover the shrub in late spring.
photos.k: What time of year do you think this was taken?

photos.t: Jim Thorpe Greeted by Mayor Gaynor
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Jim Thorpe, a Sauk and Fox athlete, won the pentathlon and decathlon at the 1912 Olympics and was greeted by New York Mayor William Gaynor in the summer of 1912. The next year Thorpe lost his medals over a technicality, and they were restored in 1983.
photos.k: Why would someone lose a medal for something minor?

photos.why: Ezra Pound was an American poet who lived in London and helped many other writers get their start. Alvin Langdon Coburn photographed him with a dramatic, intense look.
photos.k: What kind of poetry do you think he wrote?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A boy crouches beside a cow, milking it by hand. Lewis Hine photographed farm children too, since many worked from early morning with their families, long before school.
photos.k: What chores do you have each day?

photos.cr: Sundry Art - Photography Fund
photos.why: Auguste Bert photographed the great Russian dancer Vaslav Nijinsky in his role in the ballet Scheherazade around 1913. Nijinsky was famous for his leaps, which seemed to hang in the air.
photos.k: How high can you jump?

photos.t: Vaslav Nijinsky in Le Spectre de la Rose
photos.cr: Sundry Art - Photography Fund
photos.why: Auguste Bert photographed Nijinsky in the ballet Le Spectre de la Rose, The Phantom of the Rose, in 1913. He danced the ghost of a rose that a young girl had worn to a ball.
photos.k: How would you dance like a flower?

photos.t: Percy MacKaye as Alwyn, the Poet
photos.why: Arnold Genthe made an autochrome of the poet Percy MacKaye in costume as Alwyn in a masque, a kind of costume play. The picture is seen in a mirror view.
photos.k: Why would a poet dress up as a character?

photos.why: Frank Hurley photographed the ship Aurora anchored to floe ice off the Western Base in Antarctica during the 1911 to 1914 expedition of Douglas Mawson. The ship is tiny among the ice.
photos.k: Why would a ship tie up to ice?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Underwood and Underwood photographed Jim Thorpe in 1913, the year after his Olympic victories. Thorpe was a member of the Sauk and Fox Nation, and many call him the greatest all-round athlete in history.
photos.k: What sports do you think he played?

photos.why: A bright orange bull statue with flower garlands stands near a Hindu temple in Varanasi, India. Banker Albert Kahn sent photographers around the world with color Autochrome plates for his Archives of the Planet, and Stéphane Passet took this one.
photos.k: How old do you think the statue is?

photos.why: Stéphane Passet photographed Paris in color just before the First World War. The tall buildings and empty street look blue in the early light.
photos.k: Why do you think the street is empty?

photos.why: A shop in Paris with bright red and gold paint, photographed in color in 1914. Early Autochromes captured the colors of ordinary streets before they changed.
photos.k: What would you buy at a shop like this?

photos.why: Arnold Genthe photographed the actress Ann Murdock in 1914. A buzzer was a name for a small telephone-like gadget used on stage.
photos.k: What would a buzzer do in a play?

photos.why: Dutch archives hold this photograph of French troops from the colonies wearing white uniforms and red caps in 1914, at the start of World War I. Soldiers from Africa and Asia fought for France.
photos.k: Why would soldiers from far away fight in this war?

photos.t: Eiffel Tower from the Trocadéro, Autochrome
photos.why: Auguste Léon photographed the Eiffel Tower in color around 1914 for the Archives of the Planet, a project funded by the banker Albert Kahn. He wanted to record the whole world in color photographs.
photos.k: What would you put in an archive of the planet?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A woman carries a peace sign and a U.S. flag in a march in Washington, D.C., in 1914. Peace marches began as World War I started in Europe.
photos.k: What would you write on a peace sign?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: From the back window of his New York gallery, Alfred Stieglitz photographed a snow-covered tree and the buildings beyond. He made many pictures of the same view in different seasons.
photos.k: Choose a window at home. What would it look like in different seasons?

photos.cr: Gift of Arielle Kozloff Brodkey in memory of Dr. Jerald S. Brodkey
photos.why: Eugène Atget photographed the park at Saint-Cloud, outside Paris, at dawn when it was empty. Two great trees stand over a still pool that doubles them.
photos.k: What do you notice about the water?

photos.why: Frank Hurley was the photographer on Ernest Shackleton's Antarctic expedition. The ship Endurance sits frozen in sea ice under a pink sky, in an image Hurley colored by hand.
photos.k: How would you feel stuck in the ice?

photos.why: Paul Strand photographed small figures hurrying past the huge dark windows of a bank on Wall Street in New York. He made the people look tiny and the building look like a wall, and it became a landmark of modern photography.
photos.k: How do the huge windows make the people feel?

photos.why: Hurley lit the ship Endurance with flashbulbs at night, with the rigging coated in frost. Soon after, the ice crushed the ship, but all twenty-eight men survived by dragging lifeboats across the ice.
photos.k: What would you pack if you had to leave a ship in the ice?

photos.why: Flower sellers and shoppers fill the great square of Kraków in this Autochrome by Tadeusz Rząca. Autochromes made on glass look like stained glass, glowing with color.
photos.k: What do you think the people are buying?

photos.why: San Francisco held a huge world's fair in 1915 to celebrate the opening of the Panama Canal. Arnold Genthe photographed its colonnades and domes in color.
photos.k: What would you want to see at a world's fair?

photos.why: Vegetables, oranges and a jug sit on a table, glowing like stained glass. Autochrome was made on glass plates, and the colors have lasted more than a century.
photos.k: Which food do you want to eat?

photos.why: Frank Hurley photographed Ernest Shackleton's ship Endurance stuck in the ice of the Weddell Sea in 1915 from far across the floe. The ice would later crush the ship, and the crew survived on the floes for months.
photos.k: What would you do if your ship was stuck in ice?

photos.t: Hussey and James Working in the Laboratory on Endurance
photos.why: Frank Hurley photographed scientists Leonard Hussey and Reginald James working in the lab on board Endurance in 1915. Even on an expedition they did science.
photos.k: What experiments would you do on a ship?

photos.t: Looking Across Newly Formed Ice with Endurance
photos.why: Hurley photographed new ice stretching to the ship Endurance in the Weddell Sea in 1915. A thin crust of ice formed around the ship.
photos.k: What does new ice look like?

photos.why: Frank Hurley photographed a king penguin with its chick on the Shackleton expedition around 1915. King penguin chicks are fluffy and brown, and the parents keep them warm.
photos.k: Why are baby penguins fluffy?

photos.why: The U.S. Army sent soldiers into Mexico in 1916 to chase Pancho Villa. This photograph shows the 4th Field Artillery on the march.
photos.k: Why would an army carry cannons on a horse-drawn wagon?

photos.t: New Hope School, near Shawnee, Oklahoma
photos.why: Lewis Hine photographed a rural school in Oklahoma in 1916, with 31 pupils present. Hine photographed children in school as well as at work for the National Child Labor Committee.
photos.k: What would a one-room school be like?

photos.t: Ruth St. Denis in an Oriental Dance
photos.why: Arnold Genthe made an autochrome of the dancer Ruth St. Denis in a costume from The Book of Eastern Nights in 1916. She was a pioneer of modern dance in America.
photos.k: How would you dance in a long scarf?

photos.why: Arnold Genthe made a direct color photograph of the Fire Fountain at the 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition in San Francisco. The fountain was lit with colored lights.
photos.k: How would you make a fountain with fire?

photos.t: French Soldiers Resting Among the Ruins
photos.why: French soldiers rest on the rubble of a town in the war zone in 1916. Whole towns were destroyed by shelling in World War I.
photos.k: Why do soldiers rest in ruins?

photos.why: In 1917 the artist Marcel Duchamp sent a porcelain bathroom fixture, signed R. Mutt, to an art show. The judges refused to show it, so Alfred Stieglitz photographed it in his gallery. The original is lost, and this photograph is the best record of one of the most argued-about artworks ever.
photos.k: Is it art if an artist says it is? What do you think?

photos.t: A Wave of Infantry Going Over the Top
photos.why: Frank Hurley, who served as an official photographer with the Australian forces, photographed soldiers going over the top to resist a counterattack in 1917. He made composite pictures from several negatives to capture the drama.
photos.k: Why was combining negatives controversial?

photos.why: Underwood and Underwood photographed Boy Scouts in New York in 1917, when the Scouts were helping with the war effort. The picture was published in National Geographic.
photos.k: What do Scouts do to help?

photos.t: Dental Work in the Hospital, Hood Rubber Co.
photos.why: Lewis Hine photographed dental work at the hospital of the Hood Rubber Company in Cambridge, Massachusetts, in 1917. Some factories offered health care to workers.
photos.k: Why would a factory offer a dentist?

photos.why: Underwood and Underwood photographed 500 newly made bluejackets, sailors of the U.S. Navy, in 1917. They had just joined up after the United States entered the war.
photos.k: What would you wear as a sailor?

photos.why: Man Ray photographed the artist William Zorach in 1917. Zorach was a Lithuanian-American sculptor and painter.
photos.k: How does the photographer show his personality?

photos.why: Underwood and Underwood photographed a jazz band leader returning from World War I. Jim Europe's band introduced jazz to France.
photos.k: What instruments does a jazz band play?

photos.t: Carriers Gathering the Wounded Behind the Battle Line
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Stretcher bearers collect wounded soldiers behind the lines in France in 1917. This is a photograph of the work of army medics.
photos.k: What would a medic need to carry?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed the painter Georgia O'Keeffe more than three hundred times over several years. He made close-ups of her face, hands and clothing, as one long portrait.
photos.k: What do her hands tell you about her?

photos.t: Aerial View of the Ruins of Vaux, France
photos.why: Edward Steichen led aerial photography for the US Army in the First World War. His camera in an airplane showed shell craters and ruined villages that the army needed to understand.
photos.k: What can you tell about a battlefield from above?

photos.t: Machines of the Australian Flying Corps
photos.why: This photograph shows airplanes of the Australian Flying Corps in 1918, lined up. Early airplanes were made of wood and fabric.
photos.k: Why were they built from wood and cloth?

photos.why: Allied troops paraded in the Russian port of Vladivostok in 1918. After the Russian Revolution, foreign soldiers came into the country.
photos.k: Why would foreign troops march in Russia?

photos.why: This photograph shows a British 12-inch railway howitzer, a huge gun that moved on rails in World War I. Such cannons could fire shells over many miles.
photos.k: How would you move such a giant gun?

photos.why: Edward Steichen was an aerial photographer in the U.S. Army in World War I. He photographed Montfaucon in the Argonne from the air in 1918, showing the shell-torn landscape.
photos.k: Why would an army need pictures from the air?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A farewell parade for soldiers on their way to World War I fills a street in Indiana in 1918. The whole town came out to wave them off.
photos.k: How would you say goodbye to someone going to war?

photos.t: Genuine Jazz for the Yankee Wounded
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: American wounded soldiers listen to a jazz band in a Paris courtyard in 1918. Jazz was new to Europe, and soldiers loved it.
photos.k: Why would music help the wounded?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: German prisoners of war celebrate in a hospital prison camp near London in 1918. Even in captivity, prisoners kept up customs.
photos.k: How would you celebrate if you were far from home?

photos.t: A Baseball Game between the Shellshockers and the Gassers
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Wounded American soldiers play baseball between the shellshockers and the gassers in London in 1918. They were recovering from war injuries and found comfort in a game.
photos.k: Why would baseball help soldiers feel better?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: O'Keeffe lifts her hands near her face against a dark background. Stieglitz believed a portrait could be made of a person's hands as well as their face.
photos.k: What do your hands say about you?

photos.why: A colorful Autochrome frames a green garden through a stone arch at an estate near Philadelphia. The color picture shows lawn, trees and flowers in soft greens and pinks.
photos.k: What would you like to do in a garden like this?

photos.why: French soldiers stand in formation near the clock tower in Beirut, a year after the First World War. Frédéric Gadmer took the picture in color for Albert Kahn's Archives of the Planet, an effort to record the world on color plates.
photos.k: Why would someone want to preserve a picture of a regiment?

photos.why: Georges Chevalier photographed Ali Kuli Khan, the chargé d'affaires of Persia in Washington, in 1919. He was a diplomat and a translator of Bahá'í texts.
photos.k: What does a diplomat do?

photos.why: Captain Edward Rickenbacker was America's top ace of World War I, with 26 victories. He was a famous race car driver before flying.
photos.k: How did pilots shoot in early airplanes?

photos.t: The Nancy Crews Honored by Secretary Daniels
photos.why: Underwood and Underwood photographed the crews of the Navy flying boats called NC, or Nancy, honored by Secretary of the Navy Josephus Daniels in 1919. They had made the first flight across the Atlantic.
photos.k: How would you fly across an ocean in 1919?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: This photograph shows an artist's studio in Woodstock, New York, around 1919. Woodstock became an art colony in the early 1900s.
photos.k: What would you paint in a country studio?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A winter scene at Woodstock, New York, in 1919 shows sunlight on snowy hills. The art colony's artists loved the Catskill landscape.
photos.k: What colors does winter sunshine have?

photos.t: After a Snowstorm, Woodstock, New York
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Snow weighs down branches and covers roofs at Woodstock, New York, in 1919. Photographs of snowy countryside were sold as postcards.
photos.k: How do you clear snow from a roof?

photos.t: The Country Beautiful, Woodstock, New York
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A hillside near Woodstock, New York, in 1919 shows the Catskill landscape in leafy detail. The caption calls it The Country Beautiful.
photos.k: What makes a place beautiful?

photos.t: Across the Ranges, Woodstock, New York
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: This photograph looks across the ridges of the Catskills from Woodstock, New York, in 1919. Layers of hills fade into the distance.
photos.k: How does distance change the colors?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: A faint rainbow arches above the hills at Lake George, New York. Stieglitz photographed clouds, trees and skies near his family's summer home, and wanted these images to show feelings as well as places.
photos.k: How is a rainbow different from other things you photograph?

photos.why: Arnold Genthe photographed the old buildings of New Orleans's French Quarter in 1920. The arched doorway and iron lamp belong to a bar that was once famous.
photos.k: What stories could this door tell?

photos.why: Babe Ruth was the best-known baseball player in America. In 1920 he hit 54 home runs for the New York Yankees, a record that amazed fans. Here he poses in his uniform in a studio.
photos.k: How many home runs do you think a player can hit in a season now?

photos.why: Edward Steichen photographed the Paris studio of the sculptor Constantin Brancusi, with its smooth, shining pieces. Brancusi simplified shapes until they seemed to be pure forms.
photos.k: Which sculpture looks like a bird to you?

photos.why: Arnold Genthe photographed dancers in motion in the 1910s and 20s. In this color Autochrome a dancer in flowing blue and yellow fabric leaps in the dark.
photos.k: How does the dancer's cloth help show movement?

photos.why: A worker leans into a huge machine to adjust a bolt with his wrench. Lewis Hine photographed laborers as heroes, to show the skill and strength needed to run modern factories.
photos.k: What do you think he is fixing?

photos.t: The Turbine, Power-House, New York City
photos.cr: Gift of David Vestal
photos.why: Lewis Hine photographed a workman beside a giant turbine in a New York power house around 1920. Hine began photographing men at work as a hero of the machine age.
photos.k: How does a turbine make power?

photos.why: Auguste Léon made an autochrome of André Honnorat, a French politician, around 1920 for Albert Kahn's Archives of the Planet. Color portraits were rare then.
photos.k: Why would a banker pay for color photographs?

photos.why: Imogen Cunningham photographed an agave plant in close detail around 1920. She looked at plants as sculptures of line and light.
photos.k: What shapes do the leaves make?

photos.why: Imogen Cunningham photographed a water hyacinth blossom around 1920. Her plant pictures were praised for their sharp lines and soft tones.
photos.k: What does a hyacinth blossom look like up close?

photos.why: Edward Weston photographed his relative Dr. Edward B. Weston around 1920. Weston later became one of America's best-known photographers.
photos.k: Why would someone photograph a relative?

photos.why: Doris Ulmann photographed a bell ringer outside a church. Ulmann was a New York portrait photographer who traveled in the South and the Appalachians to photograph vanishing ways of life.
photos.k: What does a bell ringer do?

photos.why: Doris Ulmann photographed a man holding a bridle, the strap for guiding a horse, around 1920. Her soft-focus portraits are quiet and respectful.
photos.k: How does a bridle control a horse?

photos.why: Berenice Abbott photographed Janet Flanner, an American writer in Paris who wrote for The New Yorker, in the 1920s. Abbott made portraits of artists in Paris before she turned to documenting New York.
photos.k: What is a Paris correspondent?

photos.why: Doris Ulmann photographed an old man with a boy around 1920. A grandfather and grandson are a favorite portrait.
photos.k: What would an old man teach a boy?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Tri-State News Bureau photographed the first American Olympic ice hockey team in 1920 at the Antwerp Games. Hockey was added to the Summer Olympics that year.
photos.k: Why would hockey be in the summer Games?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Theodor Horydczak photographed the Memorial Amphitheater at Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia in the 1920s. It holds ceremonies for the nation's fallen soldiers.
photos.k: Why would a country keep a cemetery for soldiers?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Theodor Horydczak photographed a farm outside Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, in the 1920s. Later, President Dwight Eisenhower retired to a farm there.
photos.k: Why would a president want to live on a farm?

photos.t: Aerial View of the Washington Post Office and Railroad Station
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: An early aerial photograph shows Washington's main post office and Union Station, 1920. Airplanes made new views of cities possible.
photos.k: What does a city look like from above?

photos.t: Repairing Telephone Lines During a Gas Attack
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Keystone View Company photographed signal soldiers with gas masks repairing a telephone line during a gas attack on the Western Front. Communication wires were cut constantly.
photos.k: Why would a telephone line matter so much?

photos.why: A path lined with tall cypress trees leads toward the Taj Mahal in India. This early color picture shows the white marble tomb glowing pink in the light.
photos.k: Where does the path seem to lead?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed his mother Hedwig, in a rocking chair at the family's Lake George house. The deep lines of her face tell a long story.
photos.k: What might she be thinking about?

photos.why: Edward Steichen photographed the dancer Isadora Duncan performing among the columns of the Parthenon in Athens. She is a tiny figure in the huge, shadowy temple. Duncan danced barefoot in flowing robes and helped invent modern dance.
photos.k: How do the huge columns make the dancer seem?

photos.t: Drilling for a Shot: Old-Fashioned Way of Mining Coal
photos.cr: Gift of David Vestal
photos.why: Lewis Hine photographed a coal miner drilling a hole for explosives in 1921. Mining was hard and dangerous work done mostly by hand.
photos.k: How would you drill rock by hand?

photos.why: Edward Weston photographed the interior of an attic in 1921 with beams and angles in light and shadow. He was moving toward sharp-focus, simple compositions.
photos.k: How do light and shadow make shapes in a room?

photos.why: Georges Chevalier photographed Alexander Kerensky, the head of Russia's provisional government in 1917. After the revolution he lived in exile.
photos.k: What would you do if you lost your country?

photos.why: Man Ray's 1921 photograph shows a flat iron with tacks glued to its bottom. He called it Gift, and it is one of the most famous objects in Dada art.
photos.k: Why would you ruin an iron?

photos.why: Lewis Hine photographed David F. Houston, a U.S. cabinet member, in 1921. Hine also made portraits for a living.
photos.k: What does a cabinet member do?

photos.why: Auguste Léon photographed Alexandre Khatissian, a prime minister of Armenia, in 1921 as part of Albert Kahn's Archives of the Planet. Léon recorded delegates at the Paris peace conference.
photos.k: What does a peace conference do?

photos.why: Auguste Léon photographed Akaki Chkhenkeli, a Georgian statesman, in 1921. Léon recorded delegates who came to Paris.
photos.k: Why would delegates come to Paris?

photos.t: Dedication of the Liberty Memorial Site, Kansas City
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: In November 1921, a huge crowd gathered in Kansas City, Missouri, to dedicate the site of the Liberty Memorial. Allied military leaders from five countries attended.
photos.k: Why would a city build a memorial?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A woman named Selma Snook held a funeral for her dog in Washington in 1921. The newspaper photographer made it a funny but sad image.
photos.k: How would you remember a pet?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Women's clothing is modeled at a spring fashion show in New York in 1921. The hemlines and hats show the fashion of the early 1920s.
photos.k: How is the clothing different from today's?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Tree branches swirl against the sky like dancers in a picture made at Lake George. Alfred Stieglitz loved to find shapes and rhythms in nature.
photos.k: What shapes do you see in the branches?

photos.t: Music: A Sequence of Ten Cloud Photographs
photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Stieglitz photographed clouds because critics said his portraits were successful only because of his famous sitters. He wanted to show that a picture of only sky and clouds could make people feel emotions like music does.
photos.k: What kind of music would this sky play?

photos.why: Thomas Edison invented the practical electric light bulb, the phonograph and a movie camera, among over a thousand patents. In this portrait he sits calmly, in his seventies.
photos.k: What would you invent?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed the gable of a house and apple trees at Lake George, New York, in 1922. His pictures of the farm there were quiet and detailed.
photos.k: How do the apples and the gable fit together?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed a barn at Lake George in 1922. He spent summers on the family estate there and photographed what he saw around him.
photos.k: What do you notice about the barn's shape?

photos.why: Edward Weston photographed the huge steel plant of Armco in Middletown, Ohio, in 1922. The photograph made smokestacks look like monuments and led him to a new modern style.
photos.k: How can a factory look beautiful?

photos.t: Alice B. Toklas and Gertrude Stein
photos.why: Man Ray photographed the writer Gertrude Stein and her partner Alice B. Toklas in Paris in 1922. Their apartment was a gathering place for artists and writers.
photos.k: Why do artists like to meet and talk?

photos.t: Easter Egg Rolling at the White House
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Children roll Easter eggs on the White House lawn in 1922. The Easter egg roll has been a tradition for over a century.
photos.k: What would you do at an egg roll?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C., was dedicated on May 30, 1922, in front of a big crowd. Robert Todd Lincoln, Abraham Lincoln's son, attended.
photos.k: Why would the president's son attend?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Detroit Photographic Company photographed William Livingstone Jr., a Detroit businessman, in 1922. Portraits of important local people were part of the business.
photos.k: Why would a photographer make portraits of businessmen?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A shop in Washington used live models to show off hosiery, or stockings, in 1922. Women stood in the window and drew a crowd.
photos.k: How else would a store advertise?

photos.t: First Snow and the Little House
photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: A small house stands in the snow at Lake George, New York. Stieglitz photographed the same estate for years, in all seasons, making simple scenes feel quiet and personal.
photos.k: What would you do in the first snowfall?

photos.why: Herbert Ponting's 1923 book The Great White South told of the 1910 to 1913 Terra Nova expedition to Antarctica. This picture from the book shows the ice and sky.
photos.k: What would you photograph at the bottom of the world?

photos.t: The Great White South, Antarctic Scene
photos.why: Herbert Ponting's pictures of Antarctica from Captain Scott's expedition were published in a book in 1923. Ponting made some of the most famous pictures of the polar regions.
photos.k: What would you write in a polar diary?

photos.t: President Coolidge on the Speaker's Stand
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: President Calvin Coolidge speaks from a stand with Army and Navy officers in 1923. Coolidge was known as Silent Cal because he spoke so little.
photos.k: Why would a quiet president be a good speaker?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Edward S. Curtis photographed the entrance of a Yurok sweat house in California around 1923. The house was a low dwelling used by men for gathering and ceremony.
photos.k: Why would a sweat house have a small entrance?

photos.why: Leonora Hughes was an American dancer who became famous in Paris in the 1920s. Edward Steichen photographed her with a cloche hat and pearls, the style of the time.
photos.k: What do you notice about the fashion?

photos.cr: Alfred Stieglitz Collection
photos.why: Alfred Stieglitz photographed clouds in the sky for a series called Equivalents in the mid-1920s. He called them equivalents because they were equal to feelings, not pictures of things.
photos.k: What feeling does a cloud give you?

photos.why: Edward Weston photographed the Mexican painter Diego Rivera in 1924 when Weston was living in Mexico City. Rivera was known for giant murals.
photos.k: Why would a painter paint on a huge wall?

photos.t: Victorious Olympic Team Returns Aboard the S.S. America
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Members of the American team, victorious at the 1924 Paris Olympics, return aboard the S.S. America. The crowd on deck wave flags and hats.
photos.k: What would you do on the ship home from the Olympics?

photos.cr: Acquired through exchange with George Eastman House
photos.why: A mother sits near a window holding her baby, in a plain room. Lewis Hine photographed families in need for relief organizations, so people would see who they were helping.
photos.k: What would you give this family?

photos.cr: The Severance and Greta Millikin Purchase Fund
photos.why: Eugène Atget photographed a misty park near Paris in early spring. The bare trees and dim light make it feel like a quiet dream.
photos.k: What time of day do you think it is?

photos.t: A Girl in Swedish Folk Costume
photos.why: A young girl wears a white cap and a bright red, yellow and blue costume with braids. This early color photograph preserves the vivid colors of Swedish folk dress.
photos.k: Which colors in the costume stand out the most?

photos.why: In 1925 leaders from several European countries met in Locarno, Switzerland, to agree on treaties to keep peace after the First World War. This color Autochrome shows the delegation from Czechoslovakia.
photos.k: Why do you think countries have such meetings?

photos.why: In 1925 Paris held a huge fair of modern design, the exhibition that gave the Art Deco style its name. The Polish pavilion shows the clean lines and decoration that fair made famous.
photos.k: What shapes do you notice in the pavilion?

photos.why: Two dance partners pose close together in a dramatic embrace. Edward Steichen photographed celebrities for Vanity Fair and Vogue, and made dance look romantic and daring.
photos.k: What dance do you think they are performing?

photos.why: Eugène Atget photographed a fairground at the Fête du Trône in Paris around 1925. The funfair set up each spring on the edge of the city.
photos.k: What rides would be at a fair in 1925?

photos.why: Edward Weston photographed a plaster works in Los Angeles in 1925 with a close eye for shapes. He found beauty in factories and machines.
photos.k: What shapes can you see?

photos.why: Roger Dumas made an autochrome, an early color picture, of the Italian delegation at the Locarno Conference in 1925. European powers met at Locarno in Switzerland to try to keep peace.
photos.k: How could color photographs have helped in 1925?

photos.why: Eugène Atget photographed a shop window on Rue du Château des Rentiers in Paris around 1925. He took photographs of shop windows, mannequins and displays.
photos.k: What would you put in a shop window?

photos.why: Imogen Cunningham photographed a magnolia blossom in 1925. She isolated the flower against a dark background so it looks like a sculpture.
photos.k: What does a magnolia blossom remind you of?

photos.why: Roger Dumas made an autochrome of the French delegation at the Locarno Conference in 1925. The color glows softly in the picture.
photos.k: How does early color look different?

photos.why: Eugène Atget photographed a shop at the old market of Les Halles in Paris around 1925. The market fed the city for centuries.
photos.k: What would you buy at a market stall?
