photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Toni Frissell photographed Jacqueline Kennedy in 1952 for Sports Illustrated. She would become First Lady of the United States in 1961.
photos.k: What would it be like to become First Lady?

photos.why: Senator John F. Kennedy married Jacqueline Bouvier in Newport, Rhode Island, in September 1953. The photographer Toni Frissell captured the new couple leaving the church. Kennedy became president in 1961.
photos.k: What do you notice about the wedding dress?

photos.t: Jackie Bouvier and Jack Kennedy in Wedding Attire
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Toni Frissell photographed Jacqueline Bouvier and John F. Kennedy in wedding attire with members of the wedding party in Newport, Rhode Island, on September 12, 1953. Kennedy was a senator then.
photos.k: What do you notice about the formal clothes?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Toni Frissell photographed the bride and groom in Newport, Rhode Island, in 1953. About 800 guests came to the wedding.
photos.k: Why would so many guests come?

photos.t: The Newlyweds Talking at the Wedding
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Toni Frissell photographed Jacqueline Bouvier and John Kennedy talking at their wedding in 1953. Her relaxed pictures were different from stiff wedding portraits.
photos.k: How is a relaxed picture different from a posed one?

photos.t: Kennedy Wedding: Jackie Throwing the Bouquet
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Toni Frissell photographed Jackie Kennedy throwing the wedding bouquet in 1953. Guests reached up to catch it.
photos.k: Why do brides throw bouquets?

photos.why: In 1947 Jackie Robinson became the first Black player in modern major-league baseball, when he joined the Brooklyn Dodgers. He faced insults and threats, and won the first Rookie of the Year award. Here he stands with his bat, number 42, which every team has since retired.
photos.k: What does it take to be the first at something?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: John Vachon photographed a jazz festival for Look magazine in 1954 in Rhode Island. The Newport Jazz Festival began that year.
photos.k: What instruments are in a jazz band?

photos.t: Geoffrey Holder and Carmen de Lavallade
photos.why: Carl Van Vechten photographed the dancers Geoffrey Holder and Carmen de Lavallade in 1955. They were a famous dance couple.
photos.k: How do two dancers move together?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Warren K. Leffler photographed a beauty parlor in Washington, D.C., in 1957. Women sit under dryers and wait for their hair to set.
photos.k: What would you do under a hair dryer?

photos.why: At seventy-five, the photographer Imogen Cunningham photographed her own reflection in a shop window in San Francisco, through the glass, with her camera held at her waist. She made art until she was in her nineties.
photos.k: How many ways can you find yourself in a reflection?

photos.t: X-15 Attitude Control Studies at Langley
photos.cr: LRC
photos.why: NACA, the agency that became NASA, photographed a simulator at Langley in 1958 used to study how to control the X-15 rocket plane. Pilots practiced with machines before flying.
photos.k: Why practice on a simulator?

photos.t: Photographer Warren K. Leffler on a Flight Deck
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Warren K. Leffler, a U.S. News and World Report photographer, stands on the flight deck of an aircraft carrier in 1959. His camera is slung at his side.
photos.k: What would you photograph on a carrier?

photos.why: Neil Armstrong flew the X-15 rocket plane, which could reach the edge of space, before he flew Apollo. He stands beside it in his pressure suit. Nine years later, he became the first person to walk on the Moon.
photos.k: What would it be like to fly to the edge of space?

photos.why: On April 12, 1961, Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space, orbiting Earth in a spacecraft called Vostok 1 for 108 minutes. This portrait shows him with his famous broad smile.
photos.k: What would you say if you were the first person in space?

photos.why: Carl Van Vechten photographed opera singer Marilyn Horne and conductor Henry Lewis in 1961. They later married.
photos.k: What instruments does an opera need?

photos.why: Marion S. Trikosko photographed James Meredith, the first Black student at the University of Mississippi, in 1962. U.S. marshals escorted him on campus.
photos.k: What would it be like to be the first?

photos.t: John Lewis Leading a Civil Rights March
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: David S. Johnson photographed John Lewis and others leading a large civil rights march in the early 1960s. Lewis became a congressman.
photos.k: Why do people march together?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Marion S. Trikosko photographed Byron Whizzer White, Supreme Court justice, in 1962. He had been a football star.
photos.k: How can an athlete become a judge?

photos.t: Titov and Glenn at the White House with Kennedy
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Marion S. Trikosko photographed Soviet cosmonaut Gherman Titov and American astronaut John Glenn at the White House with President Kennedy in 1962. They were two of the first space travelers.
photos.k: What would you ask an astronaut?

photos.t: Fuller Brush Salesman Visiting a Home
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Marion S. Trikosko photographed a Fuller Brush salesman visiting a home in 1962. Door-to-door salesmen sold brushes and household goods.
photos.k: How is shopping different today?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Marion S. Trikosko photographed the rental service at the Hecht Company department store in Washington in 1962. Customers could rent clothes and equipment.
photos.k: What would you rent?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Danny Lyon photographed Fannie Lou Hamer in a civil rights march in Hattiesburg, Mississippi, in 1962. Hamer became a leader in the fight for Black voting rights.
photos.k: Why was voting so hard to win?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Danny Lyon photographed the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom on August 28, 1963. Roughly 250,000 people came to demand civil rights and jobs.
photos.k: Why would 250,000 people travel to one place?

photos.cr: LRC
photos.why: This photograph shows Katherine G. Johnson at her desk at NASA. She was a mathematician who calculated the orbits for John Glenn's flight and for the Apollo moon missions.
photos.k: How could a person calculate an orbit by hand?

photos.why: On August 28, 1963, about 250,000 people marched to the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C., to demand jobs and freedom for all Americans. Martin Luther King Jr. gave his "I Have a Dream" speech that day. Here marchers, including King, walk together.
photos.k: What would you have carried on a sign?

photos.t: Bomb Wreckage near the Gaston Motel
photos.why: Marion S. Trikosko photographed the wreckage near the Gaston Motel in Birmingham, Alabama, after a bombing in 1963. The motel was a headquarters for civil rights leaders.
photos.k: Why would someone attack a motel?

photos.t: A. Philip Randolph and Other Civil Rights Leaders
photos.why: Marion S. Trikosko photographed A. Philip Randolph and other civil rights leaders in the Capitol rotunda in 1963 during the March on Washington. They met with senators to push for a civil rights law.
photos.k: Why would leaders meet with lawmakers?

photos.t: Aerial View of the Crowd and Stage, March on Washington
photos.why: Marion S. Trikosko photographed an aerial view of the crowd at the Lincoln Memorial on August 28, 1963. The huge crowd stretches along the Reflecting Pool.
photos.k: What does a crowd look like from above?

photos.why: Marion S. Trikosko photographed passengers, including nuns, walking near trains at Union Station in Washington in 1963. Thousands of marchers came by train.
photos.k: How would you travel to a big event?

photos.t: Conferring on the Civil Rights March
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Leaders confer in New York about the plans for the March on Washington in 1963. An Associated Press photograph shows serious men around a table.
photos.k: How would you plan a huge march?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Marchers board buses in New York in 1963 to go to the March on Washington. Thousands of buses and trains carried them.
photos.k: What would you bring on a long bus ride?

photos.t: Marchers in the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Flip Schulke photographed marchers at the March on Washington on August 28, 1963. People held signs demanding jobs and freedom.
photos.k: What would you want to say in a march?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Bruce Davidson photographed the March on Washington in 1963. Davidson, a documentary photographer, caught the hopes of the crowd.
photos.k: What do you see on people's faces?

photos.t: March on Washington, Crowd at the Washington Monument
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Bruce Davidson photographed the crowd gathering at the Washington Monument for the March on Washington. The monument rises above the marchers.
photos.k: Why would marchers meet at the monument?

photos.t: Mother, Father and Son at the March on Washington
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: David S. Johnson photographed a family at the March on Washington in 1963. Many families brought children.
photos.k: Why would parents bring a child to a march?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A White House news photographer photographed tired marchers resting after the March on Washington in 1963. Their feet were sore after a long day.
photos.k: How would your feet feel after a march?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A White House news photographer photographed a civil rights hootenanny, a folk music gathering, in Washington in 1963. Singers like Joan Baez and Bob Dylan sang at the march.
photos.k: What songs would you sing at a march?

photos.t: Charter Planes Arriving at National Airport
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Thomas O'Halloran photographed charter planes arriving at National Airport in Washington for the Civil Rights March in August 1963. Marchers came from all over the country.
photos.k: How many planes can you count?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Thomas O'Halloran photographed the civil rights march in Washington on August 28, 1963, for U.S. News and World Report. The crowd fills the Mall.
photos.k: How do you picture a crowd of 250,000?

photos.t: Firemen Turn Hoses on Protesters, Birmingham
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Bruce Davidson photographed firemen turning high-pressure hoses on civil rights protesters in Birmingham, Alabama, in 1963. Police also used dogs, and the pictures shocked the nation and helped lead to the Civil Rights Act.
photos.k: How can pictures change people's minds?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: David S. Johnson photographed demonstrators wearing buttons that said Equal Rights in '63 at the March on Washington. The buttons show how people stated their cause.
photos.k: What would you put on a button?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: David Lowell Johnson photographed the crowd at the Washington Monument during the March on Washington in 1963. People wait in the shade of the trees.
photos.k: What would you do waiting in a crowd?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: David Lowell Johnson photographed people holding signs and marching during the March on Washington in 1963. Signs asked for jobs and an end to segregation.
photos.k: What words on a sign are the most powerful?

photos.t: Signs at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: David Lowell Johnson photographed people holding signs at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in 1963. The marchers gathered near the water.
photos.k: What do the signs say?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: David Lowell Johnson photographed the crowd gathered at the Lincoln Memorial during the March on Washington in 1963. Martin Luther King Jr. gave his I Have a Dream speech from the steps.
photos.k: What would you do if you heard that speech?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Stanley Tretick photographed the March on Washington for Look magazine in 1963. Marchers fill the grass in front of the monument.
photos.k: How does a photographer cover a huge march?

photos.t: Russell Jones, Civil Rights Activist from Ohio
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Roosevelt H. Carter photographed Russell Jones, a civil rights activist from Ohio, at the March on Washington in 1963. Carter was a Black photographer from Columbus.
photos.k: Why would a photographer from Ohio go to the march?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Roosevelt H. Carter photographed marchers beside parked buses in Washington in 1963. Buses carried marchers from across the country.
photos.k: How long might the bus trip have taken?

photos.t: Lady at the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Roosevelt H. Carter photographed a woman at the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom and the Emancipation Proclamation centennial in 1963. She wears her best clothes.
photos.k: Why would she dress up for a march?

photos.t: Martin Luther King Jr. Delivers His Address at the Lincoln Memorial
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: The Rev. Martin Luther King Jr. gave his I Have a Dream speech at the Lincoln Memorial on August 28, 1963. His words about freedom and equality are among the most famous in American history.
photos.k: What is your dream for the world?

photos.why: Marion S. Trikosko photographed James L. Farmer Jr., a civil rights leader and founder of the Congress of Racial Equality, in 1964. CORE organized the Freedom Rides.
photos.k: What do the Freedom Riders do?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Howard Brodie sketched and photographed the Senate gallery during the civil rights debate in 1964. The Senate debated the Civil Rights Act for months.
photos.k: Why would a law take months to pass?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: An estimated 30,000 civil rights marchers fill the street in front of the Alabama State Capitol in Montgomery in March 1965. They had walked from Selma over several days.
photos.k: How far would you be willing to walk for a cause?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: James Karales photographed marchers on the Selma to Montgomery civil rights march in Alabama in 1965. The marchers walked 54 miles to demand voting rights.
photos.k: Why was voting so important?

photos.t: Duke Ellington and Ella Fitzgerald Performing
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: John Vachon photographed jazz musician Duke Ellington and singer Ella Fitzgerald performing together in 1966. They were two of the greatest names in jazz.
photos.k: What makes jazz special?

photos.t: Young Men Who Have Been Drafted Wait in Line
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Warren K. Leffler photographed young men who had been drafted waiting in line to be processed in Columbia, South Carolina, in 1967. During the Vietnam War, young men were drafted into the army.
photos.k: How would you feel if you were drafted?

photos.why: On Christmas Eve 1968, astronaut William Anders photographed Earth rising above the Moon's horizon from Apollo 8. It was the first time people saw the whole Earth from deep space, a small, blue, fragile marble. The picture helped inspire the environmental movement.
photos.k: What does it feel like to see our whole planet from far away?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Yousuf Karsh photographed Senator Edward Kennedy in 1968. He was the youngest brother of John and Robert Kennedy.
photos.k: What would it be like to follow two famous brothers?

photos.t: Neil Armstrong in the Lunar Module
photos.why: After the first moonwalk, Neil Armstrong sits in the lunar module with moon dust on his suit. There are almost no pictures of Armstrong on the Moon because he carried the camera. Buzz Aldrin took this one.
photos.k: Why are there so few pictures of the first man on the Moon?

photos.why: Buzz Aldrin photographed his bootprint in the lunar soil to study how fine and powdery the dust was. Because there is no wind or rain on the Moon, the print could last for millions of years.
photos.k: What would leave a footprint on the Moon for millions of years?

photos.why: Neil Armstrong photographed Buzz Aldrin saluting the US flag on the Moon in July 1969. The flag has a stiff rod along the top so it seems to wave in a place with no air.
photos.k: Why did they need a rod to hold the flag out?

photos.why: Buzz Aldrin stands in his white suit on the gray lunar plain. In his gold visor you can see a reflection of Neil Armstrong, the photographer, and the lunar module Eagle.
photos.k: Can you find Armstrong in the reflection?

photos.t: President Nixon Tossing Out the First Pitch
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Warren K. Leffler photographed President Richard Nixon throwing out the first baseball at the Washington Senators' opening game in 1969. Presidents often throw a first pitch.
photos.k: Could you throw a first pitch?

photos.cr: MSFC
photos.why: A Saturn V rocket carrying astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin Aldrin lifts off on July 16, 1969, to begin the first mission to land people on the Moon. The rocket was taller than the Statue of Liberty.
photos.k: How loud do you think the launch was?

photos.t: Apollo 12: Surveyor III and the Lunar Module
photos.cr: JSC
photos.why: Apollo 12 astronauts photographed the Surveyor III spacecraft and their lunar module on the Moon in November 1969. Surveyor III had landed there two and a half years before.
photos.k: How did astronauts find an old spacecraft on the Moon?

photos.cr: JSC
photos.why: Pete Conrad photographed astronaut Alan Bean next to the lunar module on the Moon in November 1969. Bean later became a painter of moon scenes.
photos.k: What would you paint if you had walked on the Moon?

photos.t: Buzz Aldrin at the Lunar Landing Research Facility
photos.cr: LRC
photos.why: Astronaut Buzz Aldrin practices at the Lunar Landing Research Facility at NASA Langley. The giant frame hung machines to feel like the Moon's lower gravity.
photos.k: How could you practice for low gravity?

photos.cr: HQ
photos.why: This NASA photograph shows the Apollo 11 command module Columbia with astronauts Neil Armstrong, Michael Collins and Buzz Aldrin on the recovery ship, in July 1969. The tiny capsule carried the three men to the Moon and back.
photos.k: How would three people fit in such a small capsule?

photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: Buzz Aldrin took this photograph of a bootprint on the Moon in July 1969 during Apollo 11. It shows the fine, powdery lunar soil, and it is one of the most famous pictures in history.
photos.k: Why does a footprint stay on the Moon for so long?

photos.why: Marion S. Trikosko photographed Edward Bennett Williams, a famous Washington lawyer, in 1970. He was also the owner of the Baltimore Orioles.
photos.k: What does a lawyer do for a sports team?

photos.t: Washington Senators Baseball Team on the Field
photos.why: Marion S. Trikosko photographed the Washington Senators baseball team standing on the field in 1971. The Senators left Washington after that year.
photos.k: Why would a team leave a city?

photos.t: Artist's Concept of Apollo 15 Crew Deploying the Lunar Rover
photos.cr: JSC
photos.why: NASA made this artist's concept of the Apollo 15 crew setting up the lunar roving vehicle in June 1971. The rover let astronauts travel miles across the Moon.
photos.k: Why would astronauts need a car on the Moon?

photos.why: On December 7, 1972, the crew of Apollo 17, flying to the Moon, photographed the whole Earth in sunlight from about 29,000 kilometers away. It became one of the most widely printed photographs in history.
photos.k: Where do you think you live on this ball?

photos.why: From 1971 to 1977, the US Environmental Protection Agency hired photographers in a project called Documerica to record how Americans lived and what the environment looked like. Here a logger, or faller, works on a giant red fir in the Pacific Northwest.
photos.k: How do you think trees are cut down safely?

photos.why: Apollo 17 was the last time people walked on the Moon. The astronauts used a battery-powered Lunar Roving Vehicle, a "moon buggy," to explore far from the lander at about 11 miles an hour.
photos.k: What would you want to find on the Moon?

photos.why: Empty wooden buildings stand in a town in the West where the gold and silver ran out and the people left. This color photograph is part of the EPA's Documerica project of the early 1970s.
photos.k: What stories could these empty buildings tell?

photos.t: Downtown of an Old Mining Town, Bisbee, Arizona
photos.why: Cornelius Keyes photographed the downtown of Bisbee, Arizona, in 1972 for the EPA's DOCUMERICA project. Bisbee was a copper mining town in the hills.
photos.k: How would a mining town differ from another town?

photos.t: Copper Mines and Smelter, Inspiration, Arizona
photos.why: Cornelius Keyes photographed the Inspiration Consolidated Copper Company's mines and smelter in Arizona in 1972. Smoke rises from the plant above the desert.
photos.k: How do you separate metal from rock?

photos.t: A New Mechanical Trash Collection Method
photos.why: Cornelius Keyes photographed a new mechanical trash collection method sponsored by the Environmental Protection Agency in 1972. Trucks replaced manual pickup.
photos.k: How do you think a machine can pick up trash?

photos.why: Dick Rowan photographed Bodie, a gold-mining ghost town in eastern California, in 1972. The empty buildings stand as people left them.
photos.k: Why do people leave a town?

photos.t: The Tiger Coal Shovel, Hanna Coal Company
photos.why: This photograph from 1972 shows a huge coal shovel called The Tiger working at a strip mine of the Hanna Coal Company in Ohio. Such shovels were among the largest machines on land.
photos.k: How big would a shovel need to be to dig coal like that?

photos.why: Cornelius Keyes photographed Phoenix, Arizona, from the air in 1972 for DOCUMERICA. The city spreads across the desert in a grid.
photos.k: How does a city in a desert differ from one by the sea?

photos.why: Gene Daniels photographed a park in Oregon with giant ferns and moss in 1972 for DOCUMERICA. The park, actually called Prehistoric Park, looks like a dinosaur-era forest.
photos.k: What would you expect to see in a rain forest?

photos.t: Bank Vault in the Ruins, Bodie
photos.why: Dick Rowan photographed a bank vault standing in the ruins of an old bank at Bodie, California, in 1972. The thick vault door survived while the building around it fell.
photos.k: Why would the vault survive?

photos.t: A Bulldozer Prepares a Path for a Coal Shovel
photos.why: A bulldozer clears a path for one of the huge coal shovels in Ohio in 1972. The bulldozer looks tiny.
photos.k: How can a machine make another machine look small?

photos.t: A Coal Shovel Works into a Hillside near Cadiz, Ohio
photos.why: A giant coal shovel works into a hillside off Route 9 near Cadiz, Ohio, in 1972 as part of the DOCUMERICA project. Strip mining changed the land.
photos.k: What happens to a hillside after strip mining?

photos.why: Cotton grass, which isn't really cotton, grows in the marshes of Alaska, with white tufts like puffs of cotton. The photographer Dennis Cowals recorded it for the Documerica project.
photos.k: What do you think the tufts are for?

photos.t: Maid of the Mist, Niagara Falls
photos.why: A sightseeing boat carries visitors close to the mist of Niagara Falls. Boats have taken tourists into the spray since the 1840s.
photos.k: Would you get wet on this ride?

photos.why: In 1973, an oil shortage meant many gas stations ran out of fuel, and signs like this appeared across America. Photographers for the EPA's Documerica project recorded how the energy crisis changed daily life.
photos.k: What would you do if there were no gas for the car?

photos.why: A demonstrator holds an Impeach Nixon sign in Washington, D.C., in 1973 during the Watergate scandal. The nation was in turmoil over the break-in at the Democratic headquarters.
photos.k: Why would people want to remove a president?

photos.t: The House of Coal, in Front of City Hall, Cadiz, Ohio
photos.why: A sculpture called The House of Coal stands in front of the city hall of Cadiz, Ohio, in 1973. The town celebrated its coal heritage.
photos.k: What does a town want to show off?

photos.why: Marion Trikosko photographed Golda Meir, the prime minister of Israel, in 1973. Meir was one of the first women to lead a country in the modern era.
photos.k: What does it take to lead a country?

photos.t: Heavily Tagged Subway Car in New York
photos.why: Erik Calonius photographed a New York City subway car covered in graffiti in 1973. Street art began on the subways in the 1970s.
photos.k: Is graffiti art or vandalism?

photos.why: John Vachon photographed a Caribbean harbor in 1973 for the EPA's DOCUMERICA project. Boats float near a shoreline of houses and palms.
photos.k: What do boats in a harbor need?

photos.why: John Vachon photographed a housing development in Bayamón, Puerto Rico, in 1973 for DOCUMERICA. Rows of houses show how the city grew.
photos.k: What do planned neighborhoods look like?

photos.why: Hope Alexander photographed a landfill at Bayonne, New Jersey, on New York Bay in 1974 for DOCUMERICA. Trash was buried and covered with earth.
photos.k: What happens to trash over time?

photos.why: Marion S. Trikosko photographed Alistair Cooke in 1974. Cooke was a British-American broadcaster who hosted Masterpiece Theatre.
photos.k: What would you ask a TV host?

photos.why: In July 1975 an American Apollo spacecraft and a Soviet Soyuz spacecraft docked in orbit, and the astronauts and cosmonauts shook hands in space. At the time the two countries were rivals, so the mission was a symbol of cooperation. Here the crews pose together before the flight.
photos.k: Why was it important for rivals to work together in space?

photos.why: Two Voyager spacecraft launched in 1977 each carry a gold-plated record containing greetings in 55 languages, music, and 115 pictures of Earth for any aliens that might find them. The cover shows instructions for playing it.
photos.k: What song would you put on a record for aliens?

photos.t: President Carter, Summer in the Parks
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Warren K. Leffler photographed Jimmy Carter for the Summer in the Parks program at the White House in the 1970s. The LoC date for this image is wrong.
photos.k: Why would a president visit a park?

photos.why: Olympus Mons on Mars is the largest known volcano in the solar system, about three times as tall as Mount Everest. NASA's Viking orbiters photographed it in the 1970s and sent the pictures to Earth.
photos.k: How would you climb a mountain this big?

photos.why: William P. Gottlieb photographed trombonist Al Grey, who played with Count Basie and Duke Ellington. Gottlieb's famous jazz photographs began in the 1940s, and he later gave all his pictures to the public domain.
photos.k: What does a trombone slide do?

photos.why: This photograph from the National Archives shows African American women cultivating sugar cane by hand. Jack Delano took many pictures of farm work in the South and in Puerto Rico.
photos.k: How would you cultivate a field of cane?

photos.t: A 1980 U.S. Olympic Team Member in a Cowboy Hat
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Warren K. Leffler photographed a member of the 1980 U.S. Olympic team wearing a cowboy hat at the White House. The team, back from Lake Placid, had won gold in hockey.
photos.k: What would you wear to meet the president?

photos.t: President Carter and Rosalynn Carter with an Olympic Athlete
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Warren K. Leffler photographed President Jimmy Carter and First Lady Rosalynn Carter with a member of the 1980 U.S. Winter Olympic team. The team included the hockey players who beat the Soviets in the Miracle on Ice.
photos.k: Why was the hockey game called a miracle?

photos.t: Flight Deck of Space Shuttle Columbia
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: This NASA photograph shows the flight deck of the space shuttle Columbia, the first orbiter, which flew in 1981. Rows of switches and screens surround the commander and pilot seats.
photos.k: How many switches can you count?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Romare Bearden made paper cutouts, collages of bright colors, of a jazz scene at Montreux in Switzerland in 1982. Bearden was a great American artist who made art about music.
photos.k: How can torn paper show music?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Marilyn Church sketched Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis in court in 1982 in a case about a photographer who followed her. Courtroom artists draw because cameras are not allowed.
photos.k: Why can't cameras go in a courtroom?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: John Margolies photographed a Salvation Army building in Selma, Alabama, in 1982. Margolies photographed roadside architecture across America.
photos.k: What can a building's sign tell you?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: John Margolies photographed a drive-in movie theater in Selma, Alabama, in 1982. The big screen towers over rows of parking spots.
photos.k: Why would you watch a movie from a car?

photos.why: Challenger was the second space shuttle to fly into orbit. Shuttles were rocket-launched like a rocket and landed like airplanes, and they could carry satellites and astronauts into space again and again.
photos.k: What do you think the roaring sound is like?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Warren K. Leffler photographed astronaut Donald Deke Slayton, one of the Mercury Seven, in 1983. Slayton was grounded by a heart condition but flew in space in 1975.
photos.k: How can a person who is grounded fly later?

photos.why: In February 1984, astronaut Bruce McCandless flew freely, without a safety line, away from the space shuttle using a jet-powered backpack. He drifted more than 300 feet away, with Earth far below.
photos.k: Would you be brave enough to float in space like this?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Bernard Gotfryd photographed astronaut Gordon Cooper, one of the original Mercury Seven, in 1984. Cooper flew the last and longest Mercury mission in 1963.
photos.k: What would you think about during a day in orbit?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: John Margolies photographed a laundromat in Key West, Florida, called the Margaret Truman Launderette in 1985. The name is a joke on the president's daughter.
photos.k: How do places get funny names?

photos.t: Old Pro Golf Space Course, Ocean City, Maryland
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: John Margolies photographed a miniature golf course with a space theme, with a giant astronaut statue, in Ocean City, Maryland, in 1985. Roadside attractions copied the space age.
photos.k: What would a space-themed golf course have?

photos.why: On January 28, 1986, the space shuttle Challenger broke apart seventy-three seconds after liftoff. All seven crew members died, including Christa McAuliffe, a teacher who was going to teach lessons from space. The disaster led to major safety changes.
photos.k: What can we learn when something goes wrong?

photos.cr: Purchased with funds provided by Lucia Woods
photos.why: Frank Meadow Sutcliffe photographed children bathing in the harbor at Whitby in northern England. He photographed life in the fishing town in the late 1800s, and the picture is called Water Rats.
photos.k: Why would they be called water rats?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: This peace quilt from March 1986 was stitched by women in the United States and the Soviet Union. It carries the message For Peaceful Skies.
photos.k: Why would quilts be a good way to send a message?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Bettye Lane photographed Sally Ride, the first American woman in space, accepting an award from Ms. Magazine in New York in 1988. Ride flew on the shuttle Challenger in 1983.
photos.k: What would you tell the first woman in space?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Robert Dawson photographed a storm approaching across the desert near Nixon, Nevada, in 1989. He photographed the American West for a project called The Great Central Valley.
photos.k: What does a storm look like coming over a desert?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Otis Hairston photographed Rosa Parks with Jibreel Khazan, who as Ezell Blair Jr. was one of the Greensboro Four, in 1990. Parks had refused to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, Alabama, in 1955.
photos.k: What gives a person courage to say no?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Otis Hairston photographed the Greensboro Four at the 30th anniversary of their lunch counter sit-in on February 1, 1990. Four college students sat at a Woolworth's counter in 1960, starting sit-ins across the South.
photos.k: What does sitting still do for a cause?

photos.t: Rosa Parks at a Pathways to Freedom Event
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Rosa Parks speaks at a Pathways to Freedom event in June 1990. The civil rights hero worked for justice her whole life.
photos.k: What would you like to ask her?

photos.cr: AFRC
photos.why: NASA's Dryden flight research center got a moving-base simulator in 1990 to train pilots for the SR-71 Blackbird. Simulators let pilots practice emergencies on the ground.
photos.k: Why is a simulator safer than a real plane?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Nancy Lee Katz photographed Gordon Parks, the great photographer and filmmaker, in 1991. Parks was the first Black photographer for Life magazine and directed the film Shaft.
photos.k: What would you ask a photographer who did so many things?

photos.t: Grand Marshal Nat Gray Leading the Young Men Olympian Anniversary
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Edward K. Newman photographed Grand Marshal Nat Gray leading a parade of the Young Men Olympian Benevolent Association in New Orleans in 1991. The social aid clubs march in colorful suits with brass bands.
photos.k: What would a New Orleans parade sound like?

photos.t: Grand Marshal Harold Dudley of the Zulu Social Aid and Pleasure Club
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Edward K. Newman photographed Harold Dudley, grand marshal of the Zulu Social Aid and Pleasure Club, in New Orleans in 1992. The Zulu club leads parades during Mardi Gras.
photos.k: What do you wear to lead a parade?

photos.t: Earl Coleman Jr. at a Jazz Funeral
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Edward K. Newman photographed Earl Coleman Jr. singing at a jazz funeral in New Orleans in 1992. Jazz funerals begin with slow hymns and end with lively music.
photos.k: Why would a funeral have a band?

photos.t: Astronaut Irwin Salutes the Flag at Hadley-Apennine
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: This photograph shows Apollo 15 astronaut James Irwin saluting the American flag at the Hadley-Apennine landing site on the Moon on August 2, 1971. The lunar module and the lunar rover are beside him.
photos.k: How does a flag stand on the Moon with no wind?

photos.t: Trombone Shorty and Eddie Boh Paris
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Edward K. Newman photographed Troy Trombone Shorty Andrews and Eddie Boh Paris in New Orleans in 1994. Andrews was a child musician who became a star.
photos.k: Why do kids start playing in brass bands?

photos.why: These towering columns of gas and dust in the Eagle Nebula are a place where new stars are being born. The tallest pillar is about four light-years long. Hubble's picture, taken in 1995, became one of the most famous space photographs.
photos.k: How long would it take to travel four light-years?

photos.t: South Pole Region of the Moon as Seen by Clementine
photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: This mosaic of about 1,500 images from the Clementine spacecraft in 1996 shows the Moon's south pole. Dark craters at the pole may hold ice.
photos.k: Why would ice on the Moon be important?

photos.cr: STScI (Hubble)
photos.why: In December 1995 the Hubble Space Telescope stared at one tiny patch of dark sky for ten days, and the image released in 1996 revealed about 3,000 galaxies. It showed that the universe was far fuller than anyone had known.
photos.k: How can a dark patch have thousands of galaxies?

photos.why: Comet Hale-Bopp was one of the brightest comets in decades, visible to the naked eye for eighteen months in 1996 and 1997. Philipp Salzgeber photographed it above a tree in the evening sky.
photos.k: What would you wish for if you saw a comet?

photos.t: Linear Aerospike SR-71 Experiment, First Flight
photos.cr: AFRC
photos.why: A NASA SR-71 Blackbird takes off in 1997 carrying a test engine called the Linear Aerospike Experiment on its back. The test was for a new kind of rocket engine.
photos.k: Why put an engine on the back of a plane?

photos.t: True Color of Jupiter's Great Red Spot
photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: This 1997 image from the Galileo spacecraft shows the Great Red Spot of Jupiter in roughly true color. The spot is a storm bigger than Earth that has raged for centuries.
photos.k: What kind of storm lasts hundreds of years?

photos.t: Layers in Valles Marineris on Mars
photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: Mars Global Surveyor photographed layers of rock in the walls of Valles Marineris, a canyon on Mars that is 4,000 km long. The layers record Mars's ancient history.
photos.k: How do layers tell a planet's past?

photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: In 1998 the Hubble Space Telescope photographed glowing auroras above Jupiter's poles. Jupiter's auroras are huge and bright.
photos.k: What causes an aurora?

photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: This picture of Neptune is made from the last whole planet images that Voyager 2 took in 1989 as it flew by. The bright blue planet has dark storms and white clouds.
photos.k: What makes Neptune blue?

photos.why: Astronaut Eileen M. Collins looks through the window of the shuttle Columbia in 1999. She was the first woman to command a shuttle mission.
photos.k: What would you see out that window?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: Peter Pettus photographed participants, some carrying American flags, marching in Selma, Alabama, in 1965. The photographs were published in 1999.
photos.k: Why would marchers carry flags?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: A poster for a Freedom Train to Alabama asks for contributions for Selma voting rights marchers. Peter Pettus photographed these signs in 1965.
photos.k: How could you help from far away?

photos.t: Wright Flyer Replica in a Wind Tunnel
photos.cr: ARC
photos.why: NASA tested a replica of the Wright Flyer in the 40-by-80-foot wind tunnel at Ames in 1999. Engineers wanted to see how the plane that made the first powered flight really handled.
photos.k: Why test an old plane in a wind tunnel?

photos.why: A satellite photograph shows the Dasht-e Kavir desert in Iran, with white salt flats and ridges of sand. It is one of the driest places on Earth.
photos.k: What makes the white patches?

photos.t: F/A-18 with Weapons Ready for Mission
photos.why: A U.S. Navy photographer photographed an F/A-18 fighter jet with weapons ready for a mission in December 2001. Ground crews prepared planes on carrier decks.
photos.k: Why does a jet need a big crew on the ground?

photos.why: A satellite image from NASA shows a giant alluvial fan, a fan-shaped pile of sediment, in the Taklimakan Desert of Xinjiang, China. The branching channels look like a tree from above.
photos.k: What shapes do rivers make from above?

photos.why: The calm eye of Hurricane Isabel is surrounded by thick spiraling clouds. Astronaut Ed Lu photographed it from the International Space Station, about 250 miles above Earth.
photos.k: Why do you think the eye of a hurricane is calm?

photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: The Andromeda Galaxy is the closest large galaxy to our Milky Way, about 2.5 million light-years away. This view, taken in ultraviolet light, shows its spiral arms glowing blue and white.
photos.k: Which arm of the spiral would you want to visit?

photos.why: An artist's concept from 2003 shows a Mars Exploration Rover on the red planet. The twin rovers Spirit and Opportunity landed in January 2004.
photos.k: How would you drive a car on Mars?

photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: An artist's concept shows the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, which reached Mars in 2006 and photographed the surface in great detail. Its camera can see objects the size of a dinner table.
photos.k: How could a satellite see something so small?

photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: An artist's concept from 2003 shows the Mars Science Laboratory, later named Curiosity, at sunset on Mars. Mars sunsets look blue.
photos.k: Why would a Mars sunset look blue?

photos.why: Hubble stared at one tiny dark patch of sky for many days and found about ten thousand galaxies. The patch is so small that it would look like a grain of sand held at arm's length. Each dot is a whole galaxy with billions of stars.
photos.k: What do you think this says about how big the universe is?

photos.t: Clouds Over the Caldera, La Palma
photos.why: Clouds spill over the rim of a huge volcanic crater on La Palma, one of the Canary Islands. The pines on the slope are green and thick above the sea of cloud.
photos.k: What do you think it feels like to walk through a cloud?

photos.why: On December 26, 2004, an undersea earthquake sent giant waves across the Indian Ocean, killing more than 200,000 people in fourteen countries. This picture was taken at a beach resort as the first big wave arrived, when most people did not yet understand what was coming.
photos.k: Why is it important to have tsunami warning systems?

photos.why: This spiral galaxy, about 12 million light-years away in the constellation Ursa Major, glows with billions of stars. Hubble's picture shows the bright core and the dark lanes of dust that curl around it.
photos.k: What do the dark lanes look like to you?

photos.why: Brocken Inaglory photographed a spotted puffer fish, Arothron hispidus, bumping his camera lens in the sea off the Big Island of Hawaii in 2004. Puffers inflate themselves when frightened.
photos.k: Why does a puffer fish blow itself up?

photos.t: Cape Town, South Africa, Perspective View
photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: This 2004 picture from NASA's Shuttle Radar Topography Mission and Landsat shows Cape Town and the Table Mountain peninsula in a 3D perspective. The mountain rises behind the harbor.
photos.k: How can a satellite make a 3D view?

photos.t: Martian Landmarks Dedicated to Apollo 1 Crew
photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: NASA named hills on Mars after the crew of Apollo 1, who died in a fire on the launch pad in 1967. The Spirit rover took the pictures of the hills.
photos.k: Why would someone name a hill after a person?

photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: The Chandra X-ray Observatory made this view of the Kepler supernova remnant, the glowing cloud left by a star that exploded in 1604. The colors show different energies of X-rays.
photos.k: What would a star exploding look like?

photos.why: This dark, towering shape in the Eagle Nebula is a pillar of gas and dust where new stars are forming. Hubble photographed it and scientists nicknamed it the Fairy.
photos.k: Do you see why they call it a fairy?

photos.why: Ribbons of green and purple light dance over a snowy field near Eielson Air Force Base in Alaska. Auroras happen when particles from the Sun hit Earth's upper atmosphere.
photos.k: What color would you paint the sky?

photos.why: At the U.S. Naval Academy, graduating midshipmen toss their white caps into the air at the end of the ceremony. It is a tradition that has become a joyful snapshot of celebration.
photos.k: Can you spot a cap in mid-air?

photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: The Crab Nebula is the glowing leftover of a star that exploded in the year 1054, which astronomers in China recorded. This picture combines many Hubble Space Telescope images into one.
photos.k: How do you think a star explosion could light up space for a thousand years?

photos.t: Orbit Insertion by Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: This artist's concept shows the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter firing its engines to enter orbit around Mars in 2006. The probe slowed so Mars's gravity could catch it.
photos.k: How do you slow down in space?

photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: The Cassini spacecraft used radar to peer through the thick orange haze of Titan, Saturn's largest moon, in 2005. The radar revealed dunes, rivers and lakes of liquid methane.
photos.k: What would a lake of methane be like?

photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: The Hubble Space Telescope photographed the Sombrero galaxy in 2005. Its bright center and dark dust lane look like a hat.
photos.k: Why is it named the Sombrero?

photos.why: Huge waves smash into small fishing boats on the coast of Brittany, in France. Photographer Henri Camus captured the moment the sea blew spray high into the air.
photos.k: What would you do if you were on the shore in a storm?

photos.why: Two babies in woolly winter hats lean in for a kiss. The photograph by Yogi was shared freely on Wikimedia Commons and was chosen as a Featured Picture.
photos.k: What do you think each baby is thinking?

photos.why: Thousands of king penguins stand together on a green hillside above the sea, with chicks in brown fluff among the adults. They live on islands in the cold southern ocean.
photos.k: Can you find a fluffy chick?

photos.why: An elderly holy man called a baba, or sadhu, in Nepal wears a coiled turban and has a long white beard. Wen-Yan King photographed his deeply lined face and bright colors.
photos.k: What can you tell about his life from his face?

photos.why: Boats float along a canal lined with tall, narrow brick houses in Amsterdam, in the Netherlands. The city's ring of canals was dug in the 1600s and is now a World Heritage Site.
photos.k: What would it be like to live in a house on a canal?

photos.t: A Tibetan Woman with a Prayer Wheel
photos.why: An elderly Tibetan woman holds a prayer wheel, a spinning cylinder with prayers inside. Luca Galuzzi photographed her in a street in a bright, patterned coat.
photos.k: What would you put inside a prayer wheel?

photos.why: A male gadwall, a kind of duck, floats on blue water with its feathers in fine gray and brown patterns. Close-up photographs show details you may never notice when a duck swims by.
photos.k: How many different patterns can you count?

photos.why: This Hubble Space Telescope image from 2006 shows the galaxy NGC 1275 at the center of the Perseus cluster. Red threads of gas stretch around it.
photos.k: What do you see in the red threads?

photos.t: A Sea Squirt on Soft Coral
photos.why: Nick Hobgood photographed a colorful sea squirt on a soft coral on a reef in 2006. Sea squirts are simple filter-feeding animals that look like jewels.
photos.k: What might a sea squirt eat?

photos.why: Jon Zander photographed hoodoos at sunset in Bryce Canyon National Park in Utah in 2006. Hoodoos are tall spires of rock, shaped by frost and rain over millions of years.
photos.k: How does ice make tall rocks like this?

photos.why: An Air Force photographer photographed a B-17G Flying Fortress from World War II flying beside a B-52H Stratofortress in 2006. The two bombers were built almost 70 years apart.
photos.k: What has changed in airplanes over 70 years?

photos.t: Chaos at the Heart of Orion
photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: NASA's Spitzer and Hubble telescopes photographed the center of the Orion Nebula in 2006. Newborn stars and gas swirl in a cloud so bright you can see it in the winter sky.
photos.k: How can you see a nebula without a telescope?

photos.t: A Stellar Ripple: The Cartwheel Galaxy
photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: A false-color composite of the Cartwheel galaxy from Spitzer, Hubble, Chandra and GALEX shows a giant ring where a smaller galaxy plunged through the center. Ripples spread out like a pebble in a pond.
photos.k: How does a ring form in a galaxy?

photos.t: The Mark of a Dying Star
photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: NASA's Spitzer and ESA's Herschel telescopes photographed a dying star in the constellation Lyra, called the Ring Nebula, 2,300 light-years away. The gas shed by the star forms a glowing ring.
photos.k: What happens to a star at the end of its life?

photos.why: A bright old car is parked on a cobbled street in Trinidad, a Cuban town full of colorful colonial buildings. The town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
photos.k: Which color house is your favorite?

photos.why: A red train winds through deep snow on the Bernina Railway in the Swiss Alps. The line, which climbs through mountains and over high viaducts, is a World Heritage Site.
photos.k: Would you like to ride on this train?

photos.why: The Aletsch Glacier, in the Swiss Alps, is the longest glacier in the Alps, at about 23 kilometers. Rivers of ice flow down between the mountains in the photograph.
photos.k: What do you think a glacier feels like?

photos.why: A slim blue damselfly rests on a leaf in Osaka, Japan. Its wings are as clear as glass and its eyes are huge compared to its tiny body.
photos.k: How is a damselfly different from a dragonfly?

photos.why: A red train crosses a tall curved stone viaduct high above a Swiss gorge. The Landwasser Viaduct was built in 1902 and is part of a railway that is now a World Heritage Site.
photos.k: How would you feel crossing a bridge this high?

photos.why: Gray beech trees stand in winter light in the Mátra Mountains of Hungary, with a few leaves still clinging. The quiet forest looks almost like a painting.
photos.k: What sounds do you hear in a winter forest?

photos.why: Air Force special tactics airmen leap from an airplane over the ocean. Military photographers shoot training missions like this one.
photos.k: How would you feel stepping out of a plane?

photos.why: A tall baobab stands in Madagascar, with a giant, smooth trunk and a tuft of branches on top. Baobabs store water in their trunks and can live for centuries.
photos.k: Why does the tree look as if it is upside down?

photos.why: NASA made this view of Earth by putting together many satellite images into one sphere. Clouds, oceans and continents appear as if seen from space.
photos.k: Can you find North and South America?

photos.why: A mountain vizcacha, a rabbit-like rodent related to chinchillas, sits on a rock in Bolivia's highlands. It lives in rocky areas and has a soft coat to keep warm.
photos.k: What does it remind you of?

photos.why: Ben Tubby photographed king penguins on the West Falkland Islands in 2007. King penguins are the second-largest penguins and have bright orange patches on their necks.
photos.k: How do penguins stay warm?

photos.why: David Monniaux photographed an albino green sea turtle, Chelonia mydas, a very rare white turtle, in 2007. Without pigment the turtle looks pale pink.
photos.k: Why would a white turtle be rare?

photos.why: Hans Hillewaert photographed a male red-headed finch at Sossusvlei in the Namib desert in Namibia in 2007. The small bird has a bright red head against the dry landscape.
photos.k: How do birds find water in a desert?

photos.why: This picture of the Matterhorn was taken in 2007 from the train to the Gornergrat in Switzerland. The pyramid-shaped peak is one of the best-known mountains in the world.
photos.k: Why does the Matterhorn have such a sharp peak?

photos.t: Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía, Valencia
photos.why: Diliff photographed the Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía, an opera house in Valencia, Spain, in 2007. The futuristic building was designed by Santiago Calatrava and looks like a giant helmet.
photos.k: What does the building remind you of?

photos.why: Brocken Inaglory photographed a surfer riding a wave at Santa Cruz, California, in 2007. The surfer leans along the green wall of water.
photos.k: How does a surfer stay balanced?

photos.why: Giovanni Dall'Orto photographed fluorite crystals in the natural history museum in Milan, Italy, in 2007. Fluorite forms cubes and comes in purple, green and blue.
photos.k: What colors do you see in crystals?

photos.why: Thierry Caro photographed two gold dust day geckos fighting on a banana tree in Reunion in 2007. These bright green geckos defend their territory.
photos.k: Why would two geckos fight?

photos.t: Basilica of the Sacred Heart, Brussels
photos.why: Markus Koljonen photographed the Basilica of the Sacred Heart in Brussels, Belgium, in 2007. It is one of the largest Art Deco churches in the world.
photos.k: What does Art Deco look like?

photos.why: This photograph shows fireworks at the Nagaoka Festival in Japan in 2007. The Nagaoka fireworks display is one of the biggest in the country, with huge chrysanthemum bursts.
photos.k: How do fireworks make different colors?

photos.why: Richard Bartz photographed a queen of the carpenter ant Camponotus herculeanus in extreme close-up in 2007. Her strong jaws and eyes show in fine detail.
photos.k: What do the ant's jaws look like?

photos.cr: AFRC
photos.why: NASA photographed Apollo 11 astronaut Buzz Aldrin in 2007 with a tour guide at the Dryden Flight Research Center. Aldrin, the second person to walk on the Moon, loved to talk about space.
photos.k: What would you ask someone who has walked on the Moon?

photos.cr: AFRC
photos.why: Members of the SOFIA team gather in front of the Boeing 747 that carries a telescope. SOFIA flew above the clouds to study stars in infrared light.
photos.k: Why would a telescope fly on a plane?

photos.why: A row of red dots shows the Moon passing in front of the Sun during the eclipse of August 1, 2008. The photographer used the same camera, in one place, to record each stage.
photos.k: What would you see if you looked at the Sun? (Never do this without special glasses!)

photos.why: Giant granite boulders and palms frame a pale sandy beach on La Digue, in the Seychelles. The boulders are billions of years old.
photos.k: What would you do first on this beach?

photos.why: NASA's MESSENGER spacecraft flew past Mercury in 2008 and took color pictures. The colors have been exaggerated so scientists can see differences in the rock and dust.
photos.k: Why would scientists change the colors in a photograph?

photos.why: A little wattlebird, an Australian honeyeater, perches among bright red flowers. Its long, curved bill is perfect for sipping nectar.
photos.k: What does the bird eat?

photos.t: The Golden Gate Bridge from Baker Beach
photos.why: The Golden Gate Bridge, painted "International Orange," spans the entrance to San Francisco Bay. When it opened in 1937 it was the longest suspension bridge in the world.
photos.k: Why do you think they chose orange?

photos.why: Hans Hillewaert photographed the man orchid, Aceras anthropophora, in 2008. Each flower looks like a tiny hanging man with arms and legs.
photos.k: What does each flower look like?

photos.t: Ammonite Lamp Post at Dusk, Lyme Regis
photos.why: Michael Maggs photographed a lamp post decorated with an ammonite fossil on the Marine Parade at Lyme Regis, Dorset, in 2008. Lyme Regis is known as the Jurassic Coast because of its fossils.
photos.k: What fossils could you find on a beach?

photos.why: Tobi 87 photographed Anse Takamaka, a beach on the island of Mahé in the Seychelles, in 2008. Granite boulders and palm trees frame the clear water.
photos.k: What would you do on a beach like this?

photos.why: This photograph shows the Bridgewater Causeway and Bridgewater Bridge in Tasmania, Australia, in 2008. The causeway crosses the Derwent River.
photos.k: Why would a causeway be built across a river?

photos.why: Air Force airmen train in front of a giant fire in 2008. Firefighters practice against real flames so that they know what to do in an emergency.
photos.k: How do firefighters stay safe near flames?

photos.why: Diliff made a panorama of Cabot Square in the Canary Wharf district of London in June 2008. Three of London's tallest towers rise behind the fountain.
photos.k: How tall do skyscrapers look from the ground?

photos.t: Korean Traditional Dancer at Yongsan Fall Festival
photos.why: A traditional Korean female dancer smiles at the 2008 Yongsan Fall Festival in Seoul. She wears a hanbok, the Korean national dress.
photos.k: What colors does a hanbok have?

photos.why: Ludovic Péron photographed the sailing yacht Moonbeam, a classic design by William Fife built in 1903, at the Brest maritime festival in 2008. Its white sails fill the wind.
photos.k: What would it be like to sail on a hundred-year-old yacht?

photos.why: Uwe Aranas photographed a man of the Ifugao people in Banaue, Philippines, in 2008. The Ifugao built the famous rice terraces up the mountains.
photos.k: How would you grow rice on a mountainside?

photos.why: Tiago Fioreze photographed Caracol Falls near Canela, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, in 2008. The falls drop about 131 meters into a canyon.
photos.k: How loud do you think the falls are?

photos.t: Library of the Guimet Museum, Paris
photos.why: Athoune made a panoramic view of the library of the Guimet museum in Paris in 2008. The round room is lined with books and has a gallery and a glass ceiling.
photos.k: What would you read in a room like this?

photos.why: Diliff photographed the Albert Memorial in Kensington Gardens, London, in May 2008. Queen Victoria had it built in memory of her husband, Prince Albert.
photos.k: Why do people build memorials?

photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
photos.why: This photograph of Kerron Clement, a gold medalist in the 400-meter hurdles, was shown in an exhibit at the Annenberg Space for Photography in 2008. He ran for the United States.
photos.k: How do you jump hurdles while running?

photos.t: Test Director Monitors Move of a Test Stand
photos.cr: MSFC
photos.why: Emmett Given photographed Ernie Wright, test director, monitoring the move of a rocket test stand at NASA in 2008. Engineers moved huge structures carefully.
photos.k: How would you move a building-size machine?

photos.cr: AFRC
photos.why: NASA's Tony Landis photographed veterans of the X-15 rocket plane program reunited at Dryden in 2008. The X-15 flew higher and faster than any airplane in the 1960s.
photos.k: What would they talk about at a reunion?

photos.t: Front View of the Lunar Electric Rover
photos.cr: JSC
photos.why: Regan Geeseman photographed the front of NASA's Lunar Electric Rover in 2008, a pressurized moon vehicle with 12 wheels that rotate. Astronauts could live in it for days.
photos.k: What would you do in a moon car?

photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: The Hubble Space Telescope photographed NGC 454 in 2008, a pair of galaxies, a red elliptical and a blue irregular, that are pulling at each other. They are 100 million light-years away.
photos.k: How do galaxies collide?

photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: NASA's Spitzer Space Telescope captured a new view of a rich star-forming region in infrared in 2008. Glowing dust clouds hold thousands of stars.
photos.k: What would a sea of stars look like?

photos.why: A macro photograph of a blowfly's face shows its huge compound eyes, made of thousands of tiny lenses, and the bristly hairs on its head. J. J. Harrison made the picture by combining many photos taken at different focus depths.
photos.k: How do you think a fly sees the world?

photos.why: Mount Everest, on the border of Nepal and China, is the highest mountain on Earth, at nearly 8,850 meters. Clouds blow like a banner from its summit.
photos.k: Would you want to climb it?

photos.why: An American toad sits on a rock with golden eyes and bumpy skin. It eats insects, slugs and spiders, and sings in a long trill.
photos.k: What do you notice about its eyes?

photos.by: Alchemist-hp + Richard Bartz with focus stack
photos.why: This stair-stepped crystal was grown from the element bismuth. A thin layer of oxide on its surface makes the rainbow colors, like oil on water. The crystals grow in square spirals.
photos.k: How is it like a staircase?

photos.why: The Carina Nebula is a huge cloud of gas and dust about 7,500 light-years away where many new stars are being born. This image comes from the European Southern Observatory's telescopes in Chile.
photos.k: What do the colors and shapes remind you of?

photos.why: The Inca built the city of Machu Picchu high in the Andes mountains of Peru, around 1450. Its stone walls and terraces fit perfectly without mortar, and clouds often drift between the peaks.
photos.k: How do you think people carried stone up here?

photos.why: Nick Hobgood photographed a trumpetfish, Aulostomus maculatus, in 2009. Trumpetfish hang head down among coral and sneak up on small fish.
photos.k: Why would a long thin fish hide upside down?

photos.t: Black Hole Outflows from Centaurus A
photos.why: This image of the galaxy Centaurus A combines optical, radio and X-ray data. Jets from the black hole at its center blast out in both directions.
photos.k: What do you think a black hole's jets are made of?

photos.why: Martin St-Amant photographed Machu Picchu in Peru in June 2009 from the peak of Huayna Picchu. The Inca city, built in the 1400s, sits on a ridge in the clouds.
photos.k: How would you build a city on a mountain ridge?

photos.why: Ggia made a panorama from the mountain over Elounda toward the island of Spinalonga in Crete in 2009. The small island holds a Venetian fortress.
photos.k: Why would people build a fort on a small island?

photos.why: Brocken Inaglory photographed an ant trapped in a small piece of Colombian amber in 2009. The amber is fossilized tree resin, and the ant is preserved as if it were alive.
photos.k: How can a tree make a time capsule?

photos.why: Jörg Hempel photographed a male Tenerife lizard, Gallotia galloti, in the Canary Islands in 2009. Males have blue throats and patterns.
photos.k: What does the lizard do in the sun?

photos.why: The Hubble Space Telescope photographed NGC 6302, the Butterfly Nebula, in 2009. The nebula's wings are streams of gas shed by a dying star, and the star at its center is among the hottest known.
photos.k: Why does the cloud look like a butterfly?

photos.why: Dcubillas photographed the minaret of the Sabah State Mosque in Kota Kinabalu, Malaysia, in 2009 with swiftlets flying around it. The tall tower catches the sky.
photos.k: Why do swifts nest in tall towers?

photos.cr: HQ
photos.why: In 2009 NASA marked the 40th anniversary of Apollo 11 with a press conference. Eugene Cernan, the commander of Apollo 17 and the last person to walk on the Moon, speaks.
photos.k: How would you feel as the last person on the Moon?

photos.t: Rugged South Polar Region of the Moon
photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter made this composite of the Moon's rugged south polar region in 2009. Craters, ridges and shadows cover the pole.
photos.k: Why do craters stay dark at the pole?

photos.why: Bright orange and golden autumn colors cover a valley in northern Norway, with snowy peaks in the distance. The photographer Simo Räsänen captured it in the soft light of fall.
photos.k: What do you like best about autumn?

photos.why: A sharp mountain rises behind a blue mountain lake in the Pyrenees, on the border of France and Spain. Its two points make it one of the most recognizable peaks in the range.
photos.k: Where would you put your picnic?

photos.why: The grey crowned crane has a golden crown of stiff feathers and a red cheek patch. It lives in the grasslands of Africa, and is Uganda's national bird.
photos.k: What do you think the crown is for?

photos.why: The Aqueduct of Segovia in Spain was built about 2,000 years ago by the Romans to carry water from the mountains into the city. Its 167 arches are made of granite blocks stacked without mortar.
photos.k: How could stones stay up without glue?

photos.why: A hot-air balloon is inflated with a rainbow of colors. Cappadocia in Turkey is famous for balloon rides at sunrise over its fairy-chimney rocks.
photos.k: Which color would you like on your balloon?

photos.why: This brown, many-sided crystal is a kind of garnet called andradite. Its natural flat faces form without anyone cutting them, as atoms line up as it grows.
photos.k: How can a rock grow flat faces by itself?

photos.why: In January 2010, a satellite photographed Great Britain covered in snow, with clouds drifting over the North Sea. The picture shows the whole island at once.
photos.k: Can you find your country on a map? What would it look like from space?

photos.t: Space Shuttle Endeavour on the Launch Pad
photos.cr: HQ
photos.why: The space shuttle Endeavour stands on its launch pad, attached to its orange fuel tank and two white boosters. It was one of the last shuttles to fly before the program ended in 2011.
photos.k: What do you think the launch sounds like?

photos.why: H. Zell photographed a branched murex shell, Chicoreus ramosus, 18 cm long, from the Indo-West Pacific. The spiny shell was once used for purple dye.
photos.k: What lives inside a shell like this?

photos.why: Trachemys photographed the white blossoms of a mirabelle plum tree in 2010. In spring the whole tree is a cloud of flowers.
photos.k: What would the tree smell like?

photos.why: Luc Viatour photographed Beloeil Castle in Belgium by night in 2010. The castle reflects in its moat, lit by lights.
photos.k: What does a castle look like at night?

photos.why: Nick Hobgood photographed a branching vase sponge, Callyspongia vaginalis, on a reef in 2010. Sponges filter water through their hollow tubes.
photos.k: How does a sponge eat?

photos.why: Didier Descouens photographed a piece of copal, young tree resin, from Madagascar in 2010. Spiders, termites, ants and other insects are trapped inside.
photos.k: How do insects get trapped in resin?

photos.why: Vaido Otsar photographed the Haanja Upland in Estonia in winter in 2010 from the Suur Munamägi observation tower. Snow lies over the forest below.
photos.k: How does snow change a landscape?

photos.why: George Chernilevsky photographed a scarletina bolete mushroom, Neoboletus erythropus, in 2010. The cap is brown, the pores are red, and the flesh turns blue when cut.
photos.k: Why does the flesh turn blue?

photos.why: David Gubler photographed the Bernina Express train beside Lago Bianco in Switzerland in 2010. The railway crosses a high pass in the Alps.
photos.k: Would you like to ride a train through the Alps?

photos.why: Jakub Hałun photographed the floating torii gate of the Itsukushima Shrine on Miyajima island in Japan in July 2010. At high tide the gate seems to float on the sea.
photos.k: How does the gate look at low tide?

photos.why: Luc Viatour photographed St. Aubin's Cathedral in Namur, Belgium, in 2010. The baroque church has a domed tower.
photos.k: How many windows can you find?

photos.why: NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory photographed a coronal mass ejection from the Sun on August 1, 2010. Almost the entire Earth-facing side of the Sun erupted at once.
photos.k: What does a solar eruption do to Earth?

photos.cr: GSFC
photos.why: This NASA image released on August 5, 2010, shows a galaxy pair in a close encounter. Hubble, Spitzer and Chandra each saw different features.
photos.k: Why use several telescopes for one picture?

photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: In 2010 the Hubble Space Telescope produced the most detailed maps of Pluto then possible. The images show dark and bright patches that change over time.
photos.k: How can you map a planet from billions of miles away?

photos.why: A castle with turrets stands among autumn trees beside a still lake, mirrored in the water. Svirzh Castle is in western Ukraine.
photos.k: Would you like to live in a castle?

photos.why: The emperor dragonfly is one of the largest dragonflies in Europe. It hunts other insects in flight, and its wings are as clear as glass.
photos.k: How fast do you think it can fly?

photos.t: The Last Shuttle at the Space Station
photos.why: In July 2011, a Soyuz spacecraft flew around the International Space Station with the space shuttle Atlantis attached, and photographed it. It was the last flight of the shuttle program, and this is the only photograph of a shuttle docked at the station from the outside, from a Soyuz.
photos.k: What do you think the astronauts felt when the shuttle program ended?

photos.why: Marc Ryckaert photographed the Lange Rei canal in Bruges, Belgium, in 2011. Old brick houses line the water.
photos.k: Why are canals good for old towns?

photos.t: The Ferry Alphonse-Desjardins on the Saint Lawrence
photos.why: Cephas photographed the ferry Alphonse-Desjardins crossing the Saint Lawrence River at Quebec City in 2011. The river is wide here, and the ferry connects Quebec and Lévis.
photos.k: What do you see while crossing a river by ferry?

photos.why: Julian Herzog photographed a Christen Eagle II aerobatic biplane in 2011. The little red-and-white plane is built for stunts.
photos.k: What stunts do aerobatic planes do?

photos.why: Berthold Werner photographed the basilica of Ta' Pinu on the island of Gozo in Malta on 8 October 2011. Pilgrims come here to pray.
photos.k: Why do people travel to a church?

photos.why: Joe Ravi photographed an Air France Airbus A380 landing at Washington Dulles Airport in 2011. The A380 is the largest passenger airplane in the world.
photos.k: How many people could fit inside?

photos.why: Chensiyuan photographed the fireworks at the Singapore National Day Parade in 2011. Singapore celebrates its independence on August 9 with a huge show.
photos.k: How do fireworks light up a city?

photos.why: Arcalino photographed the view from the Rozenhoedkaai in Bruges, Belgium, in 2011 at the blue hour, the moment after sunset. Lights reflect in the canal.
photos.k: What color is the sky at the blue hour?

photos.t: A 95-Year-Old Woman with Her Pet Rooster, Havana
photos.why: Jorge Royan photographed a 95-year-old woman with her pet rooster in Havana, Cuba, in 2011. She holds the bird on her lap like a cat.
photos.k: What unusual pets have you seen?

photos.why: Paolo Costa Baldi photographed the village of Atrani on the Amalfi Coast in southern Italy in 2011. Houses climb the steep cliffs above the sea.
photos.k: How would you build a town on a cliff?

photos.why: JJ Harrison photographed a forest raven, Corvus tasmanicus, eating in Collinsvale, Tasmania, in 2011. Ravens are very clever birds.
photos.k: What tricks might a clever bird know?

photos.why: Didier Descouens photographed a red crystal of almandine garnet on gray-green schist from the Granatenkogel mountain in Austria in 2011. Garnets form deep in the earth under heat and pressure.
photos.k: What does a garnet look like when polished?

photos.why: Ggia photographed the old mud-brick city of Kharanaq in Iran in January 2011. The ancient desert village is now mostly abandoned.
photos.k: Why would people leave an old village?

photos.t: Flight Controllers During the Last Shuttle Mission
photos.cr: JSC
photos.why: Bill Stafford photographed flight controllers on console during STS-135, the last space shuttle mission, in July 2011. Mission control watched as Atlantis flew for the final time.
photos.k: How would you feel on the last day of a program?

photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: NASA's MESSENGER spacecraft made this color image of Mercury in 2011. The spacecraft was the first to orbit the planet closest to the Sun.
photos.k: What would it be like at the surface?

photos.t: Aftermath of the U.S. Tornado Outbreak
photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: A NASA satellite image shows the paths of tornadoes after the outbreak of April 25 to 28, 2011, in the southern United States. The scars show as long tracks across the land.
photos.k: How can a satellite see a tornado's path?

photos.t: Gale Crater, Future Home of Curiosity
photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: In 2011 NASA picked Gale Crater as the landing site of the Curiosity rover. The crater has a mountain in its middle with layers that record Mars's history.
photos.k: Why land beside a mountain?

photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: The Dumbbell Nebula is a glowing cloud of gas shed by a dying star about 1,200 light-years away. NASA's Spitzer and other telescopes photographed it in 2011.
photos.k: How does a dying star make a shape like this?

photos.why: A shaggy yak stands in front of the snowy Annapurna mountains in Nepal. Yaks live at high altitudes and carry loads for people trekking in the Himalayas.
photos.k: How do you think its thick coat helps?

photos.why: NASA's Mars rover Curiosity took a selfie by combining dozens of photographs from the camera at the end of its robot arm. The arm doesn't show, so the rover seems to float in its sandy landscape.
photos.k: What would you tell the rover to do next?

photos.why: Tall pillars of sandstone covered with trees rise out of mist in Zhangjiajie, in Hunan, China. The strange landscape inspired the floating mountains in the movie Avatar.
photos.k: What do the pillars remind you of?

photos.by: This Photo was taken by Wolfgang Moroder
photos.why: A gondola glides along the Grand Canal in Venice, with the domes of the church of Santa Maria della Salute behind. The city was built on islands in a lagoon, and boats are its streets.
photos.k: What would you do in a city with no cars?

photos.why: The golden columns of a Greek temple stand on a ridge above the sea in Agrigento, Sicily. Greek settlers built the temples about 2,450 years ago, and many of the columns are still standing.
photos.k: How do you think they lifted such big stones?

photos.cr: JPL
photos.why: The Sombrero Galaxy, about 28 million light-years away, looks like a wide-brimmed hat. In this view from NASA's Spitzer telescope, which sees infrared light, its ring of dust glows.
photos.k: Why do you think astronomers named it after a hat?

photos.why: Dietmar Rabich photographed historic Route 66 near Amboy, California, in 2012. The old highway runs through the Mojave Desert past empty gas stations.
photos.k: What would a road trip on Route 66 be like?

photos.why: Wilfredor photographed a nine-year-old boy on Margarita Island, Venezuela, in 2012. His face is lit by bright tropical sun.
photos.k: What do you think the boy is thinking?

photos.why: Michael Gäbler photographed the Hindenburgdamm, an 11 km causeway to the island of Sylt, with the Sylt Shuttle train in 2012. Cars drive onto the train to cross.
photos.k: Why would a train carry cars?

photos.why: A fully grown Atlas moth, Attacus atlas, photographed at London Zoo in 2012. Atlas moths are among the largest moths in the world, and their wings can span 25 centimeters.
photos.k: How big is 25 centimeters?

photos.why: Thomas Bresson made this photograph of star trails on March 14, 2012, by combining 14 two-minute exposures. As the Earth spins, the stars seem to draw arcs in the sky.
photos.k: What makes the stars move in arcs?

photos.why: Dietmar Rabich photographed the Empire State Building in New York in 2012. The Art Deco tower, finished in 1931, soars above Midtown.
photos.k: How tall is the Empire State Building?

photos.why: Wilfredor photographed a Gulf fritillary butterfly, Agraulis vanillae, on Isla Margarita in 2012. The orange wings have black marks and silver spots underneath.
photos.k: What color are its wings?

photos.t: Eiffel Tower and Pont Alexandre III at Night
photos.why: Getfunky Paris photographed the Eiffel Tower lit up at night with the gilded Pont Alexandre III in 2012. The golden lamps on the bridge reflect in the Seine.
photos.k: How do lights make a city feel different at night?

photos.why: Alvesgaspar photographed the Lys River in the center of Ghent, Belgium, in April 2012. Medieval guild houses rise along the water.
photos.k: What would you see in an old canal town?

photos.t: City Lights of the United States
photos.why: NASA made this night view of the United States in 2012 from satellite data. Cities glow like orange spiderwebs.
photos.k: What do the bright patches show?

photos.why: This photograph shows a street musician playing the didgeridoo in Santiago de Compostela, Spain, in 2012. The long wooden pipe comes from Aboriginal Australia.
photos.k: What does a didgeridoo sound like?

photos.why: Uberprutser photographed the Goliath windmill in Eemshaven, in the Groningen province of the Netherlands, in 2012. Windmills pumped water off polders, land reclaimed from the sea.
photos.k: How can a windmill pump water?

photos.why: Faj2323 made a panoramic view of the Khumbu valley above Pheriche in Nepal in 2012. The trail to Mount Everest Base Camp passes through here.
photos.k: Would you like to hike here?

photos.why: NASA astronaut Don Pettit made a composite of the star trails seen from the International Space Station in 2012. He took many long exposures and stacked them.
photos.k: How do you take star pictures from a moving station?

photos.t: Golden Gate Bridge from Vista Point, Sausalito
photos.why: Dietmar Rabich photographed the Golden Gate Bridge from the vista point in Sausalito, California, in 2012. The orange-red bridge crosses the entrance to San Francisco Bay.
photos.k: Why is the bridge painted orange?

photos.t: Orbiter Discovery on the Shuttle Carrier Aircraft
photos.cr: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
